papers.title: Temporal dissociation across the eye-brain-muscle cascade delineates a preparation window before muscle activation in subacute stroke.
papers.abstract: Upper-limb motor impairment after stroke is compounded by a disrupted sensorimotor cascade linking visual attention, cortical motor preparation, and peripheral muscle activation. Whether these stages are temporally dissociated in subacute stroke, and whether their timing carries information about the preparation and execution of a reaching action, remains unclear. Thirty subacute stroke survivors and 30 healthy controls performed a full-plane nine-grid reaching task while eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and surface electromyography (EMG) were recorded synchronously. Three neurophysiological latencies were extracted: first fixation on the target, stimulus-locked lateralized readiness potential (s-LRP) onset, and peripheral muscle activation onset. Compared with controls, patients showed a stepwise delay across the cascade, with delayed visual engagement (616.73 ms vs. 367.86 ms) and delayed peripheral muscle activation (1,080 ms vs. 605 ms) bracketing a cortical preparation window. A random-forest classifier was trained on window-level gaze-timing features, computed separately for each target-presentation and inter-target interval of the task. Under participant-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, it achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.973 (95% CI 0.958-0.984) and an accuracy of 0.918, numerically the highest among the five classifiers compared. These findings describe a quantifiable temporal organization of the sensorimotor cascade in the subacute stage of stroke and indicate that gaze timing carries discriminative information about the occurrence of an instructed reaching action. They establish a descriptive, testable framework rather than a demonstrated clinical benefit. Validation in chronic stroke and across independent samples is further required.

papers.title: Protocol-aware dual-view single-channel EEG sleep staging with improved N1 discrimination on public sleep-EDF and SHHS benchmarks.
papers.abstract: To develop and evaluate DualViewSeqSleepNet, a protocol-aware single-channel EEG model for automatic sleep staging under reproducible public benchmark settings. The model integrates raw-waveform and spectral encoders, gated epoch-level fusion, lightweight bidirectional cross-epoch aggregation, and an auxiliary loss targeting Wake-N1 and N1-N2 transitions. Primary testing used the exact Sleep-EDF SC-subset protocol of SeriesSleepNet. Secondary no-retuning evaluation used SHHS-1 healthy C4-A1 data. On Sleep-EDF, DualViewSeqSleepNet achieved macro-F1 0.821, accuracy 0.869, and Cohen's kappa 0.808, exceeding the SeriesSleepNet anchor and improving N1 F1 from 0.506 to 0.535. On SHHS-1, it reached macro-F1 0.791 and accuracy 0.854 without architecture-family retuning. Ablation and robustness analyses supported the contributions of dual-view fusion, cross-epoch aggregation, and N1-aware supervision. DualViewSeqSleepNet provides a modest, protocol-aligned improvement for public single-channel sleep staging, especially near Wake-N1-N2 boundaries, but does not establish external clinical validation or autonomous deployment readiness.

papers.title: Integrated rehabilitation for post-stroke anxiety: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke anxiety (PSA) affects approximately one-quarter of stroke survivors and impedes functional recovery, yet pharmacological options remain limited by inconsistent efficacy and absent standardized guidelines. This study evaluated an integrated rehabilitation program combining repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine for PSA. In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 188 participants with mild-to-moderate PSA were randomized 1:1 to standard care (pharmacotherapy, general care, and exercise therapy) or integrated rehabilitation (standard care plus rTMS, acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine) for 4 weeks, with an 8-week follow-up. The primary outcome was the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). Secondary outcomes included the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Activities of Daily Living (ADL), Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses followed an intention-to-treat framework. The integrated rehabilitation group showed significantly greater reductions in HAM-A scores at Week 4 than controls (between-group difference, 2.49 points; 95% CI, 1.50 to 3.48; p <0.01), and this treatment benefit was maintained at week 12 (p<0.01). In supportive analyses of the secondary outcomes, Holm-adjusted group × time interactions remained significant for PSQI, MoCA, upper-extremity motor function, ADL, and SAS scores (all adjusted p<0.05), but not for lower-extremity motor function or IADL. The integrated rehabilitation program improved the primary anxiety outcome and provided supportive evidence of broader clinical benefits in sleep quality, cognition, and upper-extremity motor function, together with distinct patterns of functional change in ADL and IADL. Overall, these findings support further consideration of this integrated approach as an adjunct to pharmacotherapy for PSA. Biological mechanisms and contributions of individual intervention components remain undetermined. Further mechanistic investigations incorporating biological measures would help clarify the underlying mechanisms. https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT05147077.

papers.title: Construction of a nomogram prediction model for symptom residue after tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in children with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome based on lasso-logistic regression analysis.
papers.abstract: To identify the factors associated with residual symptoms after adenotonsillectomy in children with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) using LASSO-logistic regression, and to construct a nomogram prediction model. A total of 324 children with OSAHS treated at our hospital from January 2023 to March 2024 were enrolled and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 227) and an internal validation cohort (n = 97) at a ratio of 7:3. According to the 1-year follow-up results, the training cohort was further divided into a recovery group and a residual symptom group. In addition, 175 children with OSAHS treated at our hospital from April 2024 to January 2025 were included as an external validation cohort. LASSO-logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative residual symptoms. A nomogram model was then established and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Compared with the recovery group, children in the residual symptom group were younger and had higher proportions of males, BMI > the 95th percentile, family history of OSAHS, asthma, rhinitis, >8 spontaneous awakenings per hour before surgery, AHI > 18 events/h before surgery, as well as higher preoperative mYPAS scores and postoperative Wong-Baker scores (all P < 0.05). LASSO-logistic regression identified sex, BMI, asthma, rhinitis, number of spontaneous awakenings before surgery, and preoperative AHI as independent predictors (all P < 0.05). The AUC values of the nomogram in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts were 0.874, 0.851, and 0.850, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA demonstrated favorable clinical utility. The nomogram showed good predictive performance and may help assess the risk of residual symptoms after adenotonsillectomy in children with OSAHS.

papers.title: Perioperative esketamine is associated with attenuated sleep deprivation-related cognitive dysfunction: a retrospective biomarker cohort study of the ferroptosis-neuroinflammation axis.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation is common in older surgical patients and may increase vulnerability to postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction through oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and regulated cell-death pathways. Experimental studies increasingly implicate hippocampal ferroptosis, particularly disruption of the SLC7A11-GSH-GPX4 defense axis, in sleep-deprivation-related cognitive injury. Esketamine has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but whether its perioperative neurocognitive benefit is associated with a ferroptosis-related molecular phenotype in clinical patients remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective biomarker cohort study of 398 adults aged 60-80 years who underwent elective major non-cardiac surgery between January 2022 and December 2025. Patients were classified according to preoperative sleep deprivation (total sleep time <4 h and sleep efficiency <70% during the night before surgery) and perioperative esketamine exposure, generating four groups: NSD-C, NSD-E, SD-C, and SD-E. The primary outcome was early postoperative cognitive decline on postoperative day (POD) 7, defined by a ≥1-SD deterioration in a composite neuropsychological Z score. In a biomarker subcohort, plasma 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE), malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), glutathione peroxidase activity, inflammatory cytokines, neuronal injury markers, and PBMC expression of GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4 were analyzed. Confounding was addressed using multivariable models and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting. Bootstrap mediation models examined a ferroptosis-related redox score and IL-6 as candidate mediators. In the cohort, cognitive decline occurred in 32.5% of sleep-deprived patients without esketamine and 17.7% of sleep-deprived patients exposed to esketamine. After adjustment, esketamine exposure in the sleep-deprivation subgroup was associated with lower odds of cognitive decline (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.92). Sleep deprivation was associated with higher 4-HNE, MDA, ACSL4, IL-6, TNF-α, and NSE and lower GSH, GPX activity, GPX4, and SLC7A11; these abnormalities were attenuated in the esketamine-exposed group. The exploratory ferroptosis-related redox score was independently associated with cognitive decline. Under the specified exploratory mediation model, the estimated total mediated proportion was 54%; this model-based decomposition does not establish causal biological mediation. Perioperative esketamine was associated with less pronounced early postoperative cognitive decline in sleep-deprived patients and a less pronounced peripheral ferroptosis-related/inflammatory phenotype.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Potential symptom management targets following transarterial chemoembolization in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: a network analysis and computer-simulation study.
papers.abstract: Potential symptom intervention targets in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) remain poorly understood. Symptom network analysis combined with computer-simulated interventions may help identify priority targets for symptom management. To examine symptom associations and explore potential symptom management targets among patients with HCC following TACE. A cross-sectional study included 312 patients with HCC. Symptoms were assessed 24-48 h after TACE using the Chinese versions of the M. D. Anderson Symptom Inventory and the primary liver cancer-specific symptom module. A Gaussian graphical model was used to examine symptom associations, while an Ising model and NodeIdentifyR algorithm were used to explore simulated symptom perturbations. Fatigue (86.5%), disturbed sleep (83.7%), and lack of appetite (75.0%) were the most prevalent symptoms. Nausea showed the highest estimated strength centrality. Hypothetical alleviation of dry mouth produced the largest model-predicted decrease in the mean number of active symptoms, whereas hypothetical aggravation of fever produced the largest increase. Nausea was the most connected symptom according to estimated strength centrality. Dry mouth and fever showed the largest model-predicted responses to alleviating and aggravating threshold perturbations, respectively. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation; they do not establish clinical treatment effects.

papers.title: Nocturnal Sweating in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is commonly associated with symptoms such as snoring and daytime sleepiness, while atypical manifestations including nocturnal sweating remain less clearly understood. The current systematic review aimed to evaluate the relationship between nocturnal sweating and OSA and to explore possible physiological mechanisms underlying this association. A systematic search identified 10 relevant studies including observational, physiological, and treatment-response investigations. The included studies varied substantially in design, patient characteristics, and methods of assessing nocturnal sweating. Early studies mainly described nocturnal sweating as a nonspecific symptom among OSA patients and failed to demonstrate consistent associations with conventional severity indices such as the apnea-hypopnea index. However, more recent studies have suggested that nocturnal sweating may be associated with hypoxemic burden, rapid eye movement (REM)-related respiratory worsening, sleep fragmentation, and sympathetic nervous system activation rather than respiratory event frequency alone. Physiological studies have demonstrated improvement in sweating after continuous or automatic positive airway pressure therapy, supporting a reversible autonomic mechanism. An exploratory meta-analysis of three comparative studies showed a non-significant increase in nocturnal sweating among OSA patients (odds ratio [OR] = 1.85; 95%CI: 0.87-3.92; I 2 = 91.7%). After exclusion of one study involving untreated moderate-to-severe OSA patients, heterogeneity decreased but the association remained non-significant (OR = 1.31; 95%CI: 0.76-2.23; I 2 = 64.7%). Overall, nocturnal sweating does not appear to represent a specific diagnostic marker of OSA itself, but it may reflect physiological consequences of untreated or severe disease in susceptible individuals.

papers.title: Effects of Circadian Disruption and Chronotype on Postural Stability During Quiet Stance.
papers.abstract: Postural control is fundamental for daily activities and is known to be sensitive to disruptions of the circadian system. The present study investigated how individual circadian alignment influences postural stability in healthy adults. In total, 39 participants wore actigraphs for 2 weeks to obtain circadian regularity and misalignment parameters: composite phase deviation (CPD), interdaily stability (IS), and intradaily variability (IV). Chronotype was assessed from corrected midsleep time on free days. Postural stability was evaluated through center of pressure (COP) trajectories recorded while the participant stood on a force platform under different sensory conditions. Postural dynamics were analyzed using both linear sway measures and recurrence quantification analysis, with particular focus on laminarity (LAM) and trapping time (TT) as indicators of postural control stability and adaptability. Higher circadian disruption, reflected by increased CPD and reduced IS, was associated with greater postural instability, characterized by increased sway magnitude and higher values of LAM and TT, suggesting more intermittent and less adaptive postural control strategies. Additionally, individuals with later chronotypes exhibited poorer postural stability compared with those with earlier chronotypes. Therefore, these findings indicate that circadian disruption is associated with alterations in postural control dynamics, potentially reducing the adaptability of the postural system. Even in healthy adults, irregular sleep-wake patterns may place the sensorimotor system in a suboptimal state, increasing vulnerability to balance impairments.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Measured Posterior Neck-Fold Thickness and Tongue-Base Thickness as Anatomical Markers in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects nearly 1 billion adults globally. Polysomnography (PSG) is the diagnostic gold standard, but it is resource-intensive. Ultrasound assessment of posterior cervical soft tissue is underexplored. To evaluate the correlations involving ultrasound-measured posterior neck-fold thickness (PNFT) and tongue-base thickness (TBT) with PSG severity indices in OSA patients. We conducted a prospective study of 77 adults with PSG-confirmed OSA. Bedside ultrasound assessed PNFT and TBT. Neck circumference (NC) and indices (apnea-hypopnea index [AHI], oxygen desaturation index [ODI], and lowest oxygen saturation [LSAT]) were recorded. In total, 38 patients had mild-to-moderate OSA, and 39, severe OSA. The NC was larger in the severe group compared to the mild-to-moderate group (41.9 versus 38.4 cm respectively; p < 0.001). Neither the PNFT (mild-to-moderate group: 9.3; severe group: 10.2 mm; p = 0.184) nor the TBT (mild-to-moderate group: 65.9; severe group: 67.5 mm; p = 0.167) differed significantly between the groups; the small observed effect size (Cohen's d = 0.31 for TBT) reflects limited precision with this sample size rather than confirmatory evidence against a true difference. The PNFT correlated weakly with the AHI (r = 0.238; p = 0.037) and LSAT (r = -0.228; p = 0.048). The TBT showed a moderate correlation with the LSAT (r = -0.424; p < 0.001) and a weak correlation with the ODI (r = 0.238; p = 0.038). Except for the TBT-LSAT association, none of these ultrasound correlations remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The TBT showed a modest, sex-independent association with the LSAT, whereas PNFT's associations with OSA severity were largely attributable to sex rather than an independent anatomical effect.

papers.title: Metrics Reflecting Cumulative Exposure to Nocturnal Hypoxia Demonstrate Promising Performance in Distinguishing between Moderate and Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index is traditionally used to classify the severity of obstructive sleep apnea; however, it does not fully capture the cumulative physiological impact of nocturnal hypoxia. Metrics that quantify integrated hypoxic exposure may provide a more accurate characterization of disease severity. The current study compared the independent association and discriminative performance of hypoxic burden, cumulative time with peripheral oxygen saturation below 90%, and oxygen desaturation frequency in distinguishing between moderate and severe obstructive sleep apnea. In total, 30 patients with moderate or severe disease were evaluated using actigraphy combined with continuous nocturnal oximetry. Separate logistic regression models adjusted for body mass index were developed. Hypoxic burden and cumulative time with peripheral oxygen saturation below 90% remained independently associated with severe disease, with odds ratios of 1.35 (95%CI: 1.05-1.75; p = 0.021) and 2.46 (95%CI: 1.03-5.90; p = 0.043) respectively, whereas desaturation frequency was not significant after adjustment (odds ratio: 1.90; 95%CI: 0.97-3.73; p = 0.061). The model including cumulative time with peripheral oxygen saturation below 90% yielded an area under the curve of 0.86 (95%CI: 0.728-0.996), while the models including hypoxic burden and desaturation frequency yielded values regarding the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve of 0.84 (95%CI: 0.698-0.989) and 0.78 (95%CI: 0.618-0.954) respectively. These findings suggest good discriminative performance of metrics reflecting cumulative nocturnal hypoxic exposure; however, formal comparisons between the ROC curves were not performed. Metrics reflecting cumulative exposure to nocturnal hypoxia demonstrated promising performance in distinguishing between moderate and severe disease, and they may contribute to risk stratification in obstructive sleep apnea.

papers.title: Actimetry-Derived Sleep and Circadian Parameters in a Population-Based Sample from São Paulo: Findings from the EPISONO Cohort.
papers.abstract: To set benchmarks for sleep estimates and for parameters of rest-activity, light exposure, and skin temperature rhythms in a cohort from São Paulo. The present study used data from the 4th edition of the São Paulo Epidemiologic Sleep Study (Estudo Epidemiológico do Sono da cidade de São Paulo, EPISONO, in Portuguese), conducted between 2018 and 2019 ( N = 769). A subset of 404 participants (60% female; mean age: 49.42 ± 14.90 years) was selected based on standardized 7-day records (5 weekdays and 2 free days). Sleep estimates, cosine-based and nonparametric parameters, were extracted and added as dependent variables in generalized linear models to investigate the effects of age, sex, body mass index, socioeconomic status, season of data collection and daylight-saving time on it. Participants aged 40 years or older had earlier sleep, circadian and light exposure timing, and reduced activity levels and amplitude. Females slept longer than males and exhibited a more stable and less fragmented rest-activity rhythm but displayed impaired patterns of exposure to light. Lower socioeconomic status was associated with poorer sleep quality yet less disrupted rhythms. Obesity was correlated with greater instability in the rest-activity rhythm. Seasonal differences revealed that sleep was shorter and later in the spring compared with winter. Our results established reference values for actimetry parameters in the largest city in Latin America and can be applied to similar urban populations. They also highlight vulnerable subgroups with impaired sleep and circadian patterns in this understudied context. These findings can inform public health policies and guide the design of personalized interventions.

papers.title: Validation of the Korean Version of the Biphasic Sleep Scale (BiSS) and Its Associations with Insomnia and Sleep-Related Cognition.
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to assess the psychometric properties of the Korean version of the Biphasic Sleep Scale (BiSS), including its factor structure, reliability, and validity, in a Korean population. An online survey was applied to the general population. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were used to explore whether the three-factor model of the BiSS was retained in the Korean context. Convergent validity was compared with the Insomnia Severity Index, the 9-Item Patient Health Questionnaire, the Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep-6, and the Adaptive Cognition and Behaviors about Sleep-6 scales. The Korean BiSS was clustered into four factors: reason, consequences, nighttime sleep disturbance, and positive aspects. The confirmatory factor analysis showed that the four-factor model fit the data better than the original three-factor model. The four-factor model showed an acceptable fit (comparative fit index [CFI] =0.903; Tucker-Lewis index [TLI] = 0.881; root-mean-square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.093; and standardized root-mean-square residual [SRMR] = 0.053), while the three-factor model showed a poorer fit (CFI = 0.772; TLI = 0.730; RMSEA = 0.140; SRMR = 0.104). Internal consistency reliability was high, with a McDonald's omega of 0.914 in the four-factor model. The total BiSS score was inversely correlated with the desired bedtime and positively correlated with insomnia severity (r = 0.12) and dysfunctional beliefs about sleep (r = 0.21). In the regression analysis, the DBAS-6 was the only significant variable, but the model only explained a small proportion of the variance (adjusted R 2 = 0.05). The four-factor model of the Korean BiSS is a reliable and valid measure for assessing people's perceptions, preferences, and habits related to biphasic sleep, which involves nighttime sleep and daytime naps.

papers.title: Directional brain-heart interaction during cognitive workload: a permutation conditional mutual information approach.
papers.abstract: The functional interaction between the central nervous system and autonomic cardiovascular regulation, commonly referred to as Brain-Heart Interaction (BHI), has gained increasing attention in neurology and psychology through the joint analysis of Electroencephalography (EEG) and Electrocardiography (ECG) signals. However, the nonlinear and time-varying nature of EEG and ECG signals requires approaches that can capture directional interactions between physiological systems. In this study, we investigated the use of Permutation Conditional Mutual Information (PCMI) for the characterization of directional BHI. First, the method was evaluated on synthetically generated coupled time series to assess its ability to detect the dominant direction of interaction. Next, PCMI was applied to simultaneous EEG and ECG recordings acquired during baseline and mental arithmetic tasks from a cohort of 36 subjects. The results show that BHI complexity increases during mental arithmetic tasks compared with baseline, supporting the role of cognitive workload in modulating brain-heart dynamics. These changes primarily involved anterior and posterior scalp regions, and affected both vagal- and sympathovagal-related HRV components. These findings demonstrate that PCMI provides a framework for studying directional BHI during cognitive tasks, and highlight its potential translational value for investigating broader brain-body interactions.

papers.title: Electrical Vestibular Stimulation in Primary and Comorbid Insomnia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a common disorder associated with impaired daytime functioning and psychiatric comorbidities such as anxiety and depression. Electrical vestibular nerve stimulation (VeNS) has emerged as a potential nonpharmacological treatment due to the vestibular system's role in sleep regulation. To evaluate the safety and efficacy of VeNS versus sham stimulation in reducing insomnia severity, improving sleep quality and quality of life, and alleviating anxiety symptoms in adults with primary or psychiatric comorbid insomnia. In total, 6 databases were systematically searched from inception to September 2025, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Randomized sham-controlled trials evaluating VeNS for insomnia were included. Random-effects models estimated mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 . Of the 5 studies included, three were on primary insomnia (n = 310) and 2, on psychiatric comorbid insomnia (n = 120). The use of VeNS significantly reduced insomnia severity index scores in both primary (mean difference [MD]: -3.42; 95%CI: -6.58 to -0.26) and psychiatric comorbid (MD: -5.51; 95%CI: -8.49 to -2.52) cases. Greater benefits were observed in younger adults. While this treatment did not significantly improve global sleep quality, it did improve quality-of-life domains including vitality, mental health, and physical functioning. Anxiety symptoms were also significantly reduced. Adverse events were mild and infrequent, with no consistent device-related serious events reported. The use of VeNS may reduce insomnia severity and anxiety with good tolerability. However, evidence is limited by small sample sizes and substantial heterogeneity. Larger, high-quality, randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Cheek Characteristics and Their Relationship with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: To investigate whether cheek appearance, posture, mobility, and pressure are associated with the presence and severity of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults. Te currents cross-sectional study included 100 adults aged 18 to 59 years, classified as controls or as having mild, moderate, or severe OSA based on type-I polysomnography. Cheek appearance/posture and mobility were assessed using the Expanded Protocol of Orofacial Myofunctional Evaluation with Scores, and cheek pressure was measured using the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument (model 2.2; IOPI Medical LLC). Descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation tests, Mann-Whitney tests, and multiple linear regression were performed at a significance level of 5%. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) was positively correlated with the body mass index (BMI) and negatively correlated with cheek appearance/posture scores, whereas cheek mobility and cheek pressure were not significantly correlated with the AHI. Across OSA severity groups, cheek appearance/posture scores differed significantly: individuals with moderate and severe OSA had lower scores than the controls. No significant between-group differences were observed for cheek mobility or pressure. In the multivariable analyses, the BMI was the only variable independently associated with the AHI. Neither cheek appearance/posture nor cheek mobility remained independently associated with the AHI after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI, and cheek pressure was also not independently associated with the AHI in the secondary model. Cheek appearance/posture was associated with OSA severity in the unadjusted analyses, but it did not remain independently associated with the AHI after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. Cheek mobility and pressure showed limited associations with OSA severity.

papers.title: Associations of Sleep Patterns With Semen Quality in Sperm Donors: Insights From Untargeted Metabolomics.
papers.abstract: Sleep problems are common but their associations with semen quality remain controversial. To investigate individual and interactive associations of sleep duration and sleep quality with semen quality. This prospective cohort included 3474 sperm donor applicants, from whom 11,427 semen samples were collected. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) was employed to assess sleep quality. Semen analysis was performed according to the World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations. Semen quality parameters were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Potential nonlinear relationships were explored using restricted cubic splines and interaction analyses were conducted to evaluate the modifying effect of sleep quality on the relationship of nighttime sleep duration with semen quality. Compared with those sleeping 7-9 h/day, men with total sleep duration < 7 h/day or nighttime sleep duration < 7 h/day had reduced sperm concentration, total sperm count, and progressive and total motility. Likewise, men with PSQI > 5 had lower levels of these semen parameters than those with PSQI ≤ 5. Dose-response analyses demonstrated inverted U-shaped relationships for sleep duration, whereas PSQI scores were linearly and negatively associated with sperm concentration and motility. After FDR correction, sleep quality significantly modified the relationships between nighttime sleep duration and sperm concentration, but not for progressive or total motility. Mediation analysis conducted in a subset of 87 participants who underwent metabolomics analyses suggested that dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, isovaleryl-L-carnitine, and cytarabine may serve as potential mediators. Short sleep duration and poor sleep quality were associated with lower semen quality, and the latter might modify the association between sleep duration and semen quality. The three metabolites may serve as potential mediators, though causal inference is limited by the observational design and self-reported sleep data.

papers.title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
papers.abstract: Chronic insufficient sleep affects cardiovascular, endocrine, immune and nervous systems and is linked to cognitive decline and increased mortality. Among habitual short sleepers, a subgroup known as natural short sleepers (NSS) report sleeping ≤ 6 h per night without experiencing subjective daytime dysfunction. However, discrepancies between subjective and objective markers of alertness raise questions about their true cognitive state. NSS have been described as high in behavioural activation, a phenotype overlapping with ADHD and mania in which dysregulation of resting-state brain arousal has been well documented. Despite these parallels, few studies have investigated the neurophysiological features of NSS. The current study examined resting-state EEG in NSS and recommended-length sleepers (RLS) during eyes-open conditions. Results showed that NSS exhibited significantly higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents, particularly in occipital areas, both markers of increased drowsiness. Although global exponent values did not differ significantly, a significant Group × Region interaction was observed and NSS showed a trend toward increasing aperiodic exponents over time, suggesting less stable wakefulness under low-stimulation conditions. These findings point to subtle neurophysiological differences in NSS, raising the possibility that their perceived resilience to short sleep may mask underlying drowsiness.

papers.title: Development of a multidimensional scale for discomfort related to personal protective equipment and its exploratory association with musculoskeletal symptoms among Korean healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic required healthcare workers (HCWs) to use personal protective equipment (PPE) for prolonged periods, raising concerns about its possible relationship with musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs). PPE-related discomfort, however, is multidimensional, encompassing both direct wearing burden and organisational aspects of its deployment. How these two dimensions relate to MSDs has rarely been examined. This cross-sectional study analysed 565 Korean physicians, nurses and medical technicians who had directly cared for patients with COVID-19. A 17-item PPE Discomfort Scale was developed and its factor structure was examined using exploratory factor analysis with oblique rotation. As an exploratory objective, cross-sectional associations between PPE-related discomfort and MSDs were examined using hierarchical modified Poisson regression, adjusting sequentially for demographic, occupational, ergonomic and psychosocial covariates. Exploratory factor analysis yielded two factors; direct wearing burden (Factor 1) and organisational vulnerability (Factor 2). The prevalence of MSDs was 37.2%, with the lower back most frequently affected (19.5%). Greater total PPE discomfort was associated with MSDs (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.60, 95% CI 1.18-2.16 in the ergonomic-adjusted model). When the two subscales were entered simultaneously, the association was observed for organisational vulnerability (1.48, 95% CI 1.14-1.93), but not for direct wearing burden (0.98, 95% CI 0.67-1.44). Sleep disturbance, traumatic experience, current smoking and ergonomic exposure were independently associated with MSDs. After further adjustment for current smoking, sleep disturbance and traumatic experience, these associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant (total score 1.28, 95% CI 0.95-1.74; organisational vulnerability 1.25, 95% CI 0.96-1.62), whereas ergonomic exposure remained associated with MSDs. The PPE Discomfort Scale identified two dimensions: direct wearing burden and organisational vulnerability, supporting a multidimensional conceptualisation of PPE-related discomfort. In exploratory analyses, organisational vulnerability showed a stronger association with MSDs, although this association was attenuated after additional adjustment. Further studies are needed to confirm the factor structure and evaluate the scale in other healthcare settings.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational medicine and toxicology (London, England)

papers.title: Association between sleep bruxism, awake bruxism, perceived stress and coping strategies among dental students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Bruxism is a common condition that can adversely affect quality of life and may be associated with tooth wear, temporomandibular disorders, and failures of dental restorations. The aim of this cross-sectional study was to investigate whether sleep bruxism (SB) and/or awake bruxism (AB) were associated with perceived stress levels and coping strategies among undergraduate dental students. The study was conducted among undergraduate dental students at Medipol University Faculty of Dentistry, Istanbul, Türkiye. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire consisting of demographic information, bruxism-related questions, the 8-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), and the 30-item Ways of Coping Inventory (WOCI). Sleep bruxism was assessed using questionnaire items based on the American Academy of Sleep Medicine criteria and a previously published epidemiological study, whereas awake bruxism was determined based on self-reported awareness of clenching or grinding during wakefulness within the previous six months. The PSS and WOCI were administered using their validated Turkish versions. Group comparisons were performed using Student's t-test and chi-square test. Binary logistic regression analyses were conducted to adjust for potential confounding factors. Of the 650 students enrolled during the 2017-2018 academic year, 570 completed the questionnaires. The mean age was 21.08 ± 2.13 years; 58.9% were female and 41.1% were male. The prevalence of sleep bruxism and awake bruxism was 57.4% (n = 327) and 39.5% (n = 225), respectively. Perceived stress levels were significantly higher in participants with sleep bruxism than in those without sleep bruxism (p = 0.011), but did not differ according to awake bruxism status (p = 0.406). Participants with sleep bruxism demonstrated higher emotion-focused, and problem-focused coping scores (all p < 0.05), whereas participants with awake bruxism showed lower problem-focused coping scores than those without awake bruxism (p = 0.018). Multivariable analyses showed that perceived stress (OR=1.034, 95% CI: 1.007-1.062), problem-focused coping (OR=1.024, 95% CI: 1.009-1.039) and emotion-focused coping (OR=1.035, 95% CI: 1.006-1.066) remained independently associated with sleep bruxism. In contrast, only problem-focused coping remained independently associated with awake bruxism (OR=0.984, 95% CI: 0.969-0.998). Within the limitations of this study, sleep bruxism was associated with higher perceived stress levels and greater use of coping strategies, whereas awake bruxism was associated with reduced use of problem-focused coping despite similar perceived stress levels. These findings suggest that sleep bruxism and awake bruxism may have different psychosocial characteristics and should be evaluated separately in future research and clinical practice.

papers.title: Healthy lifestyle is associated with lower infection incidence in type 2 diabetes: A prospective cohort study with multi-omics mediation analysis.
papers.abstract: Individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at substantially increased risk of infections, yet effective strategies for infection prevention remain limited. Although adherence to healthy lifestyles has been associated with lower infection risk in the general population, whether these benefits extend to individuals with T2DM remains unclear. Moreover, the association between the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) metrics and infection risk has not been investigated. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate associations between multidimensional lifestyle factors, Life's Essential 8 (LE8) scores, and infection incidence rate in T2DM, and to explore underlying pathways using multi-omics mediation analysis. This prospective cohort included 12,885 UK Biobank participants with T2DM (mean age 60.1 years; 30.6% female), followed for a median of 13.1 years. Exposures were adherence to a healthy lifestyle (smoking, BMI, diet, physical activity, sleep, alcohol) and LE8 score (n = 9,164). The primary outcome was total incident infections, with pneumonia, gastroenteritis, and sepsis as secondary outcomes, ascertained from hospitalization and death registries. Multivariable negative binomial regression estimated associations as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Mediation analyses were conducted using nuclear magnetic resonance metabolomics (n = 8,971; 325 biomarkers) and Olink proteomics (n = 1,078; 2,920 proteins), with candidate mediators identified via false-discovery-rate-controlled screening and effects estimated using bootstrap methods.. Ideal lifestyle adherence was associated with a 44% lower infection incidence rate (IRR 0.56, 95% CI 0.46-0.68), with similar reductions for pneumonia and sepsis. Key protective factors included never smoking, healthy BMI, adequate sleep, and physical activity. LE8 scores showed dose-dependent associations, with each 5-point increase linked to an 11% lower risk (IRR 0.89, 95% CI 0.87-0.91). Mediation analysis highlighted lipid and fatty acid metabolism, including degree of unsaturation, HDL-related lipids, and GlycA. Proteomic mediators, including TRAIL-R2 and Galectin-9, implicated inflammation and innate immunity. Maintaining an ideal lifestyle and higher LE8 scores was associated with lower infection incidence rate in T2DM, partly mediated by lipid metabolism and immune-inflammatory pathways.

papers.title: Estimating the impacts of climate distress amongst an Australian youth population.
papers.abstract: Climate change is widely recognised as the greatest threat to global health in the 21st century, with young people expected to bear a disproportionate share of its current and future impacts. Consistent with this heightened vulnerability, substantial proportions of young people worldwide report experiencing climate-related distress, yet the impact that climate change has on mental health remains underexplored. This study identified characteristics that were cross-sectionally associated with climate distress amongst a cohort of young Australians who had recently been exposed a series of climate-related events (N = 323, Mage= 20.26). Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were used for this cross-sectional analysis. Further, a longitudinal analysis was conducted using linear mixed models to estimate the impact that climate distress had on mental health symptoms (depression, stress, and anxiety), sleep quality, and substance use over a one-year period (2020-2021). Cross-sectional analyses demonstrated that females, gender-diverse individuals, and those not engaged in employment, education, or training (NEET) reported significantly higher climate distress at baseline as compared to their respective counterparts. Further, those reporting greater altruism, elevated depression and stress, and lower anxiety also reported higher levels of climate distress at baseline. Linear mixed models (LMMs) revealed climate distress was linked to increasing depression and stress symptoms, but reductions in drug use. Climate distress was not associated with anxiety, sleep quality, or alcohol consumption in LMMs. These findings demonstrate that amongst a sample of young Australians, higher climate distress tends to be experienced by those who are already disposed to poorer mental health. As such, mental health related consequences of climate change may be considered one way in which climate change exacerbates pre-existing inequalities. These findings also contribute to understanding of the potential impacts that climate distress has on mental health, justifying the need for interventions for climate distress to lessen its impact on vulnerable groups and the wider mental-health crisis as the climate crisis intensifies.

papers.title: Gut microbiota‑driven indole‑3‑propionic acid protects against sepsis‑associated encephalopathy via inhibiting BNIP3L ubiquitination and restoring BNIP3L‑dependent mitophagy as a potential molecular mechanism.
papers.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe refractory neurological complication occurring in up to 70% sepsis patients with no targeted therapies. Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), a tryptophan metabolite, exerts neuroprotective effects, but its therapeutic mechanism against SAE remains unclear. BNIP3L-linked mitophagy and mitochondrial quality control are disrupted in septic neurons, while the potential correlative connection between IPA abundance and BNIP3L abundance remains undefined. This study aimed to explore the gut-brain axis mechanism and molecular target of IPA in treating SAE. We established cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) SAE mouse models with fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and exogenous IPA intervention; performed in vitro LPS-stimulated HT22 hippocampal neuronal experiments; enrolled a prospective clinical cohort of 111 ICU sepsis patients. 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted/targeted metabolomics, fiber photometry Ca2+ recording, transmission electron microscopy, Western blot, co-immunoprecipitation and linkage-specific ubiquitin ELISA were adopted. Statistical analyses included one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlation, multivariate logistic regression and ROC curve analysis. Sepsis induced gut dysbiosis, reduced tryptophan-metabolizing bacteria and depleted endogenous IPA; FMT restored microbial homeostasis and IPA, improving mouse survival, cognitive function and reducing neuronal apoptosis. Clinically, plasma IPA was significantly lower in SAE patients, positively correlated with GCS scores, and exhibited excellent diagnostic value (AUC = 0.891). In CLP mice, IPA supplementation was accompanied by lower systemic inflammatory cytokine concentrations, partial normalization of aberrant EEG power spectra, attenuated excessive Ca2+ activity in hippocampal CA1 neurons, reduced neuronal loss, improved mitochondrial ultrastructural morphology, and parallel recovery of tissue ATP levels and antioxidant capacity. In HT22 cells, LPS exposure coincided with reduced BNIP3 levels, collapsed mitochondrial membrane potential, suppressed mitophagy and elevated neuronal apoptosis; IPA treatment correlated with parallel improvements in these cellular indicators. Mechanistically, global hippocampal total K48-linked polyubiquitin abundance exhibited an inverse correlation with circulating IPA concentrations, a trend that indirectly suggests potential shifts in BNIP3 ubiquitination profiles during sepsis, though protein-specific modification could not be confirmed herein. Circulating gut-microbiota-derived IPA concentrations showed inverse covariation with total hippocampal K48-linked polyubiquitin abundance, concurrent with parallel shifts in mitophagy-related molecular markers and less severe neuronal injury across clinical and preclinical SAE cohorts; direct evidence for BNIP3L-specific K48 ubiquitination modification was absent in this work in both clinical and preclinical SAE cohorts. IPA shows reliable diagnostic performance for SAE. Collectively, our multi-layer observational data collectively reveal a correlative gut metabolite-BNIP3L-mitochondrial homeostasis signature, which only provides preliminary associative evidence to guide future translational research targeting septic cerebral injury on sepsis-induced cerebral injury. Chinese Clinical Trials Registry, registration number ChiCTR2200067084, prospectively registered before participant enrollment.

papers.title: Evaluation of Antiseizure Potential of Rufinamide and Celecoxib Combination in a PTZ-Kindled Mouse Model Through Electrophysiological, Neurobehavioral, and Molecular Analyses.
papers.abstract: Pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced kindling is a well-established experimental model for investigating epileptogenesis and evaluating the therapeutic potential of antiseizure drugs and their novel combinations. The current study investigated whether rufinamide (RUF) and celecoxib (CEL) administered individually and in combination during PTZ-kindling acquisition, attenuate seizure progression and associated neurobehavioral, biochemical, histopathological, and molecular alterations in PTZ-kindled mice. Male mice received 11 injections of PTZ at the dose of 40 mg/kg on alternate days along with daily treatment of RUF, CEL, or RUF + CEL throughout the 21-day kindling protocol. Seizure severity was monitored using behavioral seizure scoring and validated by electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings of cortical epileptiform activity. The results demonstrated that RUF alone and RUF + CEL combination versus PTZ-kindled mice significantly attenuated seizure progression and reduced epileptiform EEG discharges (p < 0.01). Behavioral assessments revealed that treated animals exhibited reduced anxiety-like behavior along with improved cognitive performance (p < 0.05-0.001). In addition, depression-like behavior evaluated by the sucrose preference test was significantly improved (p < 0.01). Biochemical analyses indicated reduced lipid peroxidation (MDA) and enhanced antioxidant defenses including SOD, GPx, and CAT, with normalization of AChE activity (p < 0.05). Furthermore, RUF and CEL treatment significantly downregulated the expression of TNF-α, IL-1β, and GFAP, indicating attenuation of neuroinflammatory responses. Histopathological outcomes further supported these findings, demonstrating preservation of neuronal architecture and increased neuronal persistence in the hippocampal subregions. Collectively, these findings suggest that the RUF + CEL combination provides enhanced protection against PTZ-induced epileptogenesis and its associated neurobehavioral and neuropathological alterations, potentially through complementary modulation of neuronal excitability, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammatory pathways.

papers.title: Neuromodulation of cortical networks facilitates motor generalization of balance training in older adults.
papers.abstract: Motor generalization, the ability to transfer learned motor skills to untrained contexts, declines with aging and limits the functional benefits of rehabilitation. Although transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) has been implicated in neuroplasticity, its potential to facilitate motor generalization and associated cortical network reorganization in older adults remains unclear. Forty community-dwelling older adults (69.2 ± 4.3 years) were randomly assigned to receive either tVNS (n = 20) or sham stimulation (n = 20) during stabilometer balance training. Motor generalization was assessed on the day following training using an untrained foam-stance task. Postural regulation was characterized using center-of-pressure (COP) measures, stabilogram diffusion analysis, a composite control index (CCI), and sample entropy (SampEn). Cortical network organization was examined using beta-band electroencephalography (EEG) functional connectivity and minimum spanning tree (MST) analysis. Compared with sham stimulation, tVNS-assisted training produced greater improvements in COP area, accompanied by changes in postural dynamics, CCI, and SampEn. MST analyses revealed increased leaf fraction and reduced average eccentricity and network diameter, although baseline-adjusted analyses provided the most consistent support for average eccentricity. Exploratory correlations further showed that changes in average eccentricity were associated with changes in critical displacement and CCI after false discovery rate correction. These findings suggest that tVNS-assisted balance training may enhance short-term transfer of postural learning in older adults, accompanied by cortical network topology reorganization. The observed neural-behavioral associations support the functional relevance of network changes but do not establish a causal mediating mechanism.

papers.title: Jujuboside A from Ziziphus: Chemistry, mechanistic pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and formulation roadmap toward neuroactive translation.
papers.abstract: Jujuboside A (JuA) is a dammarane-type triterpenoid saponin and a principal quality marker of Ziziphi spinosae semen (ZSS) and selected Ziziphus taxa. This review aimed to integrate current evidence on JuA chemistry, central nervous system (CNS) pharmacology, pharmacokinetics (PK), metabolism, safety, analytical standardization, and formulation strategies toward neuroactive translation. Evidence relevant to these domains was synthesized and critically organized to define the chemical, pharmacological, pharmacokinetic, quality-control, and formulation profile of JuA. JuA is characterized by a jujubogenin aglycone linked to a branched oligosaccharide chain, while comparative Ziziphus saponins, including JuB, JuC, protojujubosides, and jujubogenin, clarify how glycosylation influences amphiphilicity, stability, and disposition. Mechanistic evidence is strongest for CNS-related effects, particularly GABAergic modulation, neuroinflammatory restraint, mitochondrial and synaptic protection, and sleep- or stress-linked behavioral outcomes. JuA shows low oral exposure, with an oral bioavailability of approximately 1.32% and rapid stepwise deglycosylation to JuB and jujubogenin, supporting a metabolite-driven pharmacodynamic model. Standardization should integrate authenticated botanical sourcing, ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) or charged-aerosol detection/quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance (CAD/qNMR) quantification, chemometric fingerprints, and contaminant controls. Lipid-based systems, cyclodextrin complexes, and amorphous solid dispersions should be evaluated for their capacity to protect labile glycosidic linkages, sustain supersaturation, and improve exposure to pharmacologically relevant species. Key priorities are direct receptor engagement, brain-region exposure mapping, PK/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) alignment, standardized clinical-grade materials, and early human studies using objective sleep endpoints.

papers.title: Chronopharmaceutics of In Situ Gel-Based Drug Delivery Systems in the Treatment of Nocturnal Asthma: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Nocturnal asthma (NA) is characterized by airway resistance and inflammation that peak between 02:00 and 06:00, driven by circadian fluctuations in vagal tone, cortisol, and inflammatory mediators. Conventional inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting β₂-agonist combinations and oral therapies may not reliably cover this window because of suboptimal adherence, heterogeneous lung deposition, and variable systemic exposure after oral dosing. In situ gels (ISGs), which are liquids that gel after administration, have been proposed as platforms for sustained nasal or pulmonary drug delivery. To review the circadian mechanisms of NA, the formulation science of stimuli-responsive ISGs, and the evidence for their use as chronotherapeutic systems in NA. This narrative review synthesizes literature on the molecular clock and circadian pathophysiology of asthma, polymer selection and gelation mechanisms, nasal and pulmonary delivery, pharmacokinetics and safety, and manufacturing and regulatory considerations. Evidence was classified by type (in vitro or ex vivo, animal, computational, or human) and as established, preclinical, or hypothetical. Thermosensitive poloxamers, pH-responsive carbopol/chitosan systems, ion-activated gellan gum, and enzyme-degradable matrices can form mucoadhesive depots, but their gelation behaviour, mechanical stability, mucociliary clearance, and tolerability depend on formulation composition and test conditions. Hybrid architectures (nanoparticle-embedded, nanomicelle-forming, and mesoporous silica ISGs) may allow release kinetics to be separated from cellular uptake. Sustained release over several hours has been shown for gel formulations in vitro. No study has evaluated a chronotherapeutic ISG in nocturnal asthma, and benefits for airway function and adherence remain undemonstrated. Afternoon or evening dosing of inhaled corticosteroids has clinical trial support and is the main alternative chronotherapeutic strategy. Data on repeated nightly dosing and on bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration are lacking. Chronotherapeutic ISGs are a plausible but untested approach to nocturnal asthma. Priorities for translation are studies that measure drug exposure across the 02:00-06:00 window, bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration, and the safety of repeated nightly dosing. Regulatory, manufacturing, biomarker-responsive, and digital-integration concepts remain exploratory.

papers.title: Impact of exercise dose on depression and mood in patients with lung cancer: a systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses.
papers.abstract: There is a lack of standardized exercise advice for patients with depression after lung cancer. This study evaluated the effects of high-compliance and low-compliance exercise interventions, as well as different exercise methods and dosages, on the depressive mood of lung cancer patients. We conducted a comprehensive literature search in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, covering the time period from the creation of these databases to April 2026. According to the recommendations of the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM), the study was divided into the high-ACSM-compliance group and the low-ACSM-compliance group, and the effects of ACSM compliance on depression, anxiety, fatigue, and sleep in lung cancer patients were analyzed. A paired, network and dose-response meta-analysis was conducted using a random-effects model to analyze the impact of exercise on depression in lung cancer patients. We used the confidence level (CINeMA) in the network meta-analysis framework to assess the certainty of the evidence. A total of 16 randomized controlled trials were included, involving 1127 participants. Overall, exercise significantly improved depression in lung cancer patients by -0.63 (95% CI, -0.88 to -0.38; I2 = 72%, P < 0.00001). Compared with the low-compliance group, the high-ACSM group showed greater improvement (SMD, -0.81 vs -0.38). Network meta-analysis showed that aerobic exercise had the highest degree of impact on depression in lung cancer patients (SMD, -1.30, 95% CI [-2.08, -0.51]). According to CINeMA, the confidence level of aerobic exercise is low. Furthermore, when the total exercise dose reaches 601.72 metabolic equivalent-task-min/week, a significant improvement in depression in lung cancer patients can be observed. Compared with patients with low compliance, exercise intervention in high-compliance ACSM guidelines is more effective in improving depression in lung cancer patients. There is low-quality evidence suggesting that aerobic exercise may be an effective treatment for depression in lung cancer patients. There is a response relationship between nonlinear dose-total exercise volume and the depression level of lung cancer patients.

papers.title: Potential and pitfalls of artificial intelligence to address disparities in epilepsy.
papers.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and health care offers unprecedented opportunities to address global disparities in access to specialized epilepsy diagnosis and treatment, particularly in resource-limited settings. Advances in AI models, combined with increasing internet connectivity and smartphone usage in low-income and middle-income countries, offer promising solutions for epilepsy diagnosis and monitoring through AI-based analysis of electroencephalography recordings captured with affordable open-source systems, smartphone data and electronic health records. However, this technological revolution raises important questions about the preservation and expansion of clinical expertise, AI algorithm transparency and health-care equity. In this Review, we examine how AI can help to address disparities and improve global epilepsy care while maintaining high clinical standards and addressing systemic challenges.

papers.title: Dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of temporal lobe seizures with impaired consciousness.
papers.abstract: Focal temporal lobe seizures often lead to impaired consciousness. Recent work has shown depressed cortical arousal, with slow waves and decreased cortical acetylcholine as a possible mechanism for impaired consciousness in focal seizures. However, the role of other key subcortical arousal systems such as dopamine is largely unknown. We aimed to address this gap by investigating dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of focal limbic seizures with impaired behavioral responsiveness. We induced focal limbic seizures by brief electrical hippocampal stimulation in awake head-fixed mice with hippocampal and cortical local field potential recordings. Behavior was assessed by a conditioned auditory response task. We measured cortical dopamine with a genetically encoded fluorescent sensor via fiber photometry. Activity of dopaminergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) was recorded by calcium measurements. Focal hippocampal seizures were associated with altered cortical electrophysiological activity and impaired behavioral responsiveness. During seizures, we found sustained increases in dopamine in both medial prefrontal and orbital frontal cortex. We also found increased dopaminergic neuronal activity in the VTA during seizures. Despite these sustained increases, transient task-evoked dopaminergic increases in both cortex and VTA were reduced during seizures. Behavioral responses during seizures were reduced, and auditory stimuli without behavioral responses elicited smaller transient VTA dopaminergic signals compared to stimuli with preserved responses. Together, those results reveal distinct dysregulation of dopamine dynamics across sustained and fast time scales during focal limbic seizures. The sustained increases in dopamine suggest that the altered cortical function and impaired consciousness in focal limbic seizures may more closely resemble encephalopathy or delirium than deep sleep. Depressed transient dopamine release with sensory stimuli could also contribute to impaired behavioral responsiveness during seizures. Further work on the role of dopamine could have important therapeutic implications for altered cognition and behavior in people with epilepsy.

papers.title: Preliminary findings of high-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation on depressive symptoms and cognitive function in adolescents with mood disorders.
papers.abstract: Mood disorders in adolescents significantly impair their educational attainment and daily functioning. Nevertheless, there is a paucity of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pharmacological interventions specifically for adolescents, and pharmacological interventions often require a considerable duration to achieve therapeutic efficacy. High-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS), a non-invasive and safe neuromodulation technique, has demonstrated promising outcomes in the treatment of depressive symptoms in adults. Given its favorable efficacy and safety profile, Hi-tACS warrants investigation as a potential therapeutic strategy for adolescent mood disorders. A total of 27 adolescents (aged 14-18 years) diagnosed with a depressive episode of a mood disorder were enrolled and assigned to either a Hi-tACS intervention group (tACS group) or a medication treatment management group (MTM group). The tACS group received ongoing pharmacotherapy concomitant with 20 sessions of Hi-tACS intervention, administered twice daily over 10 days. The MTM group received ongoing pharmacotherapy alone. Baseline data were collected at enrollment, and follow-up assessments were conducted at 10- and 30-day post-baseline, encompassing measures of clinical symptoms (e.g., depression, anxiety, sleep quality) and cognitive function. The tACS group demonstrated significantly greater and more rapid reductions in both Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) scores (P = 0.001) and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) scores (P = 0.002) compared to the MTM group. Regarding cognitive function, although the time × group interaction effect for the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) total score (P = 0.113) did not reach statistical significance, the tACS group exhibited a notable but non-significant trend toward superior cognitive improvement relative to the MTM group. As a novel, safe, and efficient neuromodulation technique, Hi-tACS may offer enhanced efficacy in ameliorating symptoms of depression and anxiety among adolescents compared to medication alone. Furthermore, it demonstrates a potential trend toward superior cognitive enhancement, particularly in memory function.

papers.title: TGAN-TSR: A type-aware graph attention time-spectral representation for heterogeneous fusion networks in gear system fault diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Rotating machinery often demonstrates complex dynamic behaviors, such as nonstationarity, multicycle coupling, and nonlinear coherent frequency components, under different operating conditions. Nevertheless, most existing fault diagnosis methods overlook the intrinsic correlations between heterogeneous features, resulting in incomplete information representation and the loss of critical fault signatures. These limitations impede their application in high-precision fault diagnosis tasks. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Type-aware Graph Attention Network integrating Temporal and Spectral Representations (TGAN-TSR), which incorporates feature-level fusion to enhance feature modeling and discriminative capabilities for rotating machinery fault diagnosis. Advanced signal processing techniques are initially used to extract dominant frequency band components. Together with higher-order spectral analysis, frequency coupling relationships are revealed to construct time-frequency representations that capture the intrinsic characteristics of vibration signals. Subsequently, a dual-channel feature extraction framework is developed to learn deep discriminative features from both temporal and spectral domains, thus enhancing the representation of critical fault patterns. Finally, a type-aware fusion mechanism is introduced, which, combined with a graph-based modeling strategy, facilitates associative learning and hierarchical fusion of multi domain features. Extensive experiments conducted on both public benchmark datasets and a proprietary gearbox dataset demonstrate that the proposed TGAN-TSR effectively captures important fault features and significantly improves diagnostic accuracy. This method provides a reliable and interpretable diagnostic framework for the intelligent operation and maintenance of complex rotating machinery systems.

papers.title: From snoring to obstructive sleep apnea: A narrative review of pathophysiology, clinical implications and multimodal management.
papers.abstract: Snoring is a highly prevalent acoustic phenomenon generated by vibration of the upper airway soft tissues during sleep. Long regarded as a benign social nuisance, it is increasingly recognised as a clinically informative manifestation of upper airway dysfunction. In adults it is still defined almost exclusively by subjective report, since standardised objective acoustic criteria remain unestablished; this definitional weakness explains much of the extreme heterogeneity of prevalence estimates, which range from 2% to 83% across studies. Pathophysiologically, snoring reflects an imbalance between a collapsible pharynx and the mechanisms defending its patency. Framing it within the endotypic model developed for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), collapsibility, muscle responsiveness, arousal threshold and loop gain, clarifies why the snoring-upper airway resistance syndrome-OSA continuum holds for many patients but not for all, and why apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) thresholds capture only part of the clinical picture. We argue that so-called "isolated" snoring may be less inert than assumed: respiratory-effort-related microarousals provide a plausible mechanism for insomnia-like symptoms in a subset of symptomatic snorers, while observational and experimental data suggest potential links between snoring, autonomic activation and cardiometabolic risk. These relationships remain incompletely established, particularly in the absence of documented OSA, and should not be interpreted as evidence of causality. Diagnostic assessment should follow a pre-test probability-based, stepwise logic integrating history, upper airway examination, sleep testing and, in selected patients, drug-induced sleep endoscopy and airflow phenotyping, the latter promising but not yet validated for routine use. Management is correspondingly phenotype-driven. We conclude that the field's central task is the transition of snoring from a self-reported symptom to a measurable physiological trait, a prerequisite for precision-based care and for identifying, among snorers, those in whom further physiological and cardiometabolic evaluation may be warranted.

papers.title: Dreaming during anaesthesia and the wakefulness of sleep paralysis: a question anaesthesia can help answer. Comment on Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 506-24.
Video-Based Automated Seizure Classification Using Multimodal Large Language Models.
papers.abstract: Accurately distinguishing between epileptic seizures (ES) and nonepileptic seizures (NES) remains a significant clinical challenge, typically requiring resource-intensive inpatient video-EEG monitoring. We developed a multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based framework for automated extraction of semiological features from seizure videos, followed by classification of events as ES or NES. We analyzed 90 seizure videos (45 ES, 45 NES) from 29 patients in an epilepsy monitoring unit. Each event was labeled using expert-reviewed video-EEG and annotated for 24 clinically relevant semiological features. An MLLM framework integrating open-source vision-language models (VLMs) and audio-language models (ALMs) was used to extract these features automatically. The extracted features were then used to train classifiers (K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, and Deep Factorization Machine) to distinguish ES from NES. Model performance was evaluated using leave-one-patient-out (LOPO) cross-validation. Expert-annotated features yielded near-perfect classification using KNN (precision = 0.92, recall = 0.92, F1-score = 0.92, AUC = 0.99). Compared to expert annotations, the MLLM pipeline achieved a mean recall of 0.71, accuracy of 0.58, and F1-score of 0.51 for feature extraction. Using MLLM-extracted features, the KNN classifier (k = 7) achieved a precision of 0.77, recall of 0.76, F1-score of 0.76, and AUC of 0.76, correctly identifying 68 out of 90 events. Multimodal large language models can extract clinically relevant semiological features from seizure videos and support interpretable classification of ES versus NES. This approach offers a scalable, explainable tool to assist in video-based epilepsy diagnosis.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Guided Personalized Nutrition for Prediabetes in Primary Care: A Simulation-Based Technical Feasibility Study and Pragmatic Trial Protocol.
papers.abstract: Background/ObjectivesPersonalized nutrition may support a healthy lifestyle and improve prediabetes management, but most digital tools remain open loop. We developed a clinician-governed digital-twin framework for adaptive nutrition decision support and a prospective clinical evaluation pathway.MethodsThe framework integrates continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), heart-rate variability (HRV), activity, sleep, and dietary data within an individualized state-space model. Technical/computational feasibility was assessed using one deterministic 42-day reference simulation and six additional prespecified 42-day phenotype/failure stress scenarios (seven scenarios in total). Synthetic generation rules, random seeds, estimator settings, action constraints, and executable reference code are specified for reproduction. A future 24-week, three-arm multicentre pragmatic randomized trial with an embedded four-week micro-randomized component is specified using SPIRIT 2025 and SPIRIT-AI principles. No human participant was enrolled in the simulation component.ResultsIn the 42-day reference run, 126 nominal decision opportunities were generated and 97 (77.0%) met the prespecified availability rule. Thirty-five adaptive recommendations were delivered, 52 available decisions resulted in no adaptive change, 29 decisions were withheld for insufficient inputs, and 10 candidate actions were blocked by hard constraints and routed to fallback; no hard-constraint violation was delivered. CGM missingness was 5.65%. A programmed 10-minute CGM lag was recovered as 10 minutes; alignment reduced CGM-to-latent-state RMSE from 3.53 to 3.01 mg/dL, and the UKF/RTS glucose-state RMSE was 1.17 mg/dL (1.26 mg/dL within missing-CGM windows). All seven scenarios (reference plus six additional stress conditions) completed without numerical failure or delivered hard-constraint violations.ConclusionsThe results support end-to-end software-integration feasibility under explicitly programmed synthetic conditions and provide a reproducible basis for prospective validation. They do not establish physiological validity, clinical effectiveness, or safety. The future trial has not commenced or enrolled participants; prospective registration, ethics approval, final statistical review, and informed consent will precede enrollment.

papers.title: Bilateral stellate ganglion blocks for refractory ventricular arrhythmia in a patient with a left ventricular assist device and temporary right ventricular assist device (bi-ventricular assist device configuration).
Occupational exposures and cancer risk associated with the practice of urology: A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Cancer is the leading cause of death (171,630 deaths in 2022), with a rising incidence (433,000 new cases in France in 2023). A recent US study identified cancer as the leading cause of death among surgeons, suggesting an association with occupational constraints and lifestyle. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, covering the period up to April 2026. The selected articles were analyzed qualitatively to identify the various risks to which surgeons are exposed and to assess the position of urology among the surgical specialties evaluated. A total of 98 articles were identified, of which 24 were included. Occupational exposure-related risk factors were identified in the literature. Some are associated with operating-room activity and exposure to known carcinogenic agents, including surgical smoke (containing aromatic hydrocarbons and biological particles), volatile anesthetic agents, and ionizing radiation. Others relate to chronic stress, sleep deprivation, night work, and prolonged working hours. Limited awareness of these risks, inadequate medical follow-up, and potential delays in screening are also reported. Improved awareness of these occupational risks may support the development of preventive strategies for urologic surgeons.

papers.title: Does Lifetime Lung Function Influence the Development of Obstructive Sleep Apnoea?
Sleep characteristics, glymphatic proxies, and ATN biomarkers in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Sleep and glymphatic dysfunction are increasingly recognized as contributing factors to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. This study examined both the main and interactive effects of sleep characteristics and glymphatic proxies on ATN biomarkers across the AD continuum. This cross-sectional study included 325 participants (50-86 years, 36% male) who underwent 18F-Florbetapir and 18F-Flortaucipir PET/MRI. We assessed sleep characteristics by obtaining habitual sleep duration and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Neuroimaging-derived glymphatic proxies were choroid plexus volume fraction (CPVF), perivascular space volume fraction (PVSF), and free water within cerebral white matter (WMFW). Linear regression was used to examine the main and interactive associations of sleep characteristics and glymphatic proxies with ATN biomarkers. Prolonged sleep duration was associated with greater temporal tau burden (β = 0.25) and thinner cortical thickness (CTh, β = -0.19, both p < 0.01). Higher WMFW was associated with greater global Aβ burden (β = 0.20), greater temporal tau burden (β = 0.22), and thinner CTh (β = -0.41, all p < 0.01). Higher CPVF was associated with greater temporal tau burden (β = 0.15), and higher PVSF was associated with thinner CTh (β = -0.14, both p < 0.05). Notably, WMFW consistently moderated the associations between sleep duration and ATN biomarkers (|t| range = 2.61 to 2.78, q < 0.05). These findings support a role for sleep-glymphatic interactions in shaping AD pathology and suggest that this interplay warrants further investigation in longitudinal studies.

papers.title: Is GDF-15 the Missing Link Between Intermittent Hypoxia, Carotid Body Plasticity, and Cardiometabolic Disease?
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a worldwide epidemic and is strongly associated with cardiometabolic comorbidities such as hypertension, arrhythmias and heart failure. Its principal cardiovascular pathological driver is chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH). CIH induces maladaptive plasticity in the carotid body (CB), the main peripheral oxygen sensor. Profound nitro-oxidative stress and localized inflammation lead to relentless sympathetic overactivity and autonomic imbalance, causing persistent CB hyperactivity. Although this chemoreflex arc is well-characterized, the molecular messengers linking local hypoxemic stress to systemic cardiovascular decline are poorly defined. We propose that Growth Differentiation Factor-15 (GDF-15) is a very likely candidate for this bridge. GDF-15 is a well-established cardiovascular prognostic biomarker. It is strongly upregulated by hypoxia, oxidative stress and HIF stabilization. Plasma GDF-15 is related to the severity of OSA, nocturnal hypoxemia and arrhythmogenic remodeling, and is progressively reduced in clinical settings after continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. In addition to being a systemic biomarker, we speculate that local production of GDF-15 in the oxidative CB microenvironment may have autocrine / paracrine effects that maintain glomus cell hyperexcitability but this remains to be proven experimentally. Also, circulating GDF-15 may act on brainstem GFRAL receptors to enhance chemoreflex drive. We emphasize that this peripheral to central axis, localized CB signaling is a theoretical model that should be tested directly in the lab. Ultimately, therapeutic targeting of this GDF-15 axis at the CB-brainstem interface may provide a life-changing strategy to ameliorate complications of sleep-disordered breathing.

papers.title: The relationship between regularity of nighttime rest behavior and depressive symptoms in everyday home-life using smartphone-based sensor data.
papers.abstract: Depression is associated with disruptions in circadian and behavioral rhythms.
