Beyond sleep duration, temporal consistency of sleep-related behavior may represent a relevant aspect of behavioral rhythms. We examine nighttime rest regularity derived from passive smartphone activity data and its association with depressive symptom severity. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) scores and self-reported sleep duration were collected via smartphones from 234 individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD; n = 95) or healthy controls (HC; n = 139). Step counts from a 15-day window surrounding BDI assessment were analysed for nighttime intervals (10 pm-8 am), requiring at least seven valid nights. Group differences and associations between nighttime rest regularity, sleep duration, and depressive symptom severity were examined. No significant MDD-HC differences in rest regularity emerged (all p ≥ .058), although estimates descriptively suggested lower nighttime consistency (NCI: β = -0.083) and greater rest-duration variability (LRI-SD: β = 0.118) in MDD. Within MDD, lower regularity corresponded descriptively to higher BDI scores, but no associations survived correction (all p-BH ≥ 0.154). LRI-SD showed the largest positive estimate (β = 0.086, p-BH = 0.154). Self-reported sleep duration was not significantly associated with BDI scores in MDD (β = 0.045, p = .662) or rest regularity variables (|β| ≤ 0.043, all p ≥ .236). Smartphone step count data enable multi-day characterization of nighttime rest regularity. No significant associations with self-reported sleep duration emerged, suggesting distinct behavioral characteristics. Associations with depressive symptom severity showed small descriptive tendencies but remained nonsignificant after correction, warranting investigation.

papers.title: Cold adaptation enhances sustained alternative thermogenic mechanisms to counteract obesity in mice.
papers.abstract: Non-shivering thermogenesis (NST), traditionally attributed to brown adipose tissue (BAT), accounts for a substantial fraction of energy expenditure (EE) below thermoneutrality. Comparing obesity-prone C57BL/6J (B6) mice, which rely on BAT, with obesity-resistant A/J mice, which preferentially recruit alternative mechanisms, probably including muscle NST, we sought to determine whether the understudied muscle-based NST contributes to strain-specific obesity resistance. Mice underwent 2-week cold acclimation (CA) and rewarming, or were maintained at thermoneutrality on a standard or high-fat diet. Continuous indirect calorimetry assessed EE and core body temperature (Tb). At the end of CA, the gastrocnemius muscle was analysed by integrated multi-omics approaches, and muscle performance was evaluated using in vivo force-frequency measurements and treadmill exercise calorimetry. We found that (i) circadian Tb rhythmicity was transiently attenuated in A/J mice during the first week of CA, (ii) CA increased EE more in A/J than in B6 mice, (iii) rewarming rapidly abolished most CA-induced elevation of EE in both strains, although a small yet significant elevation persisted in A/J mice, and (iv) CA increased the energetic cost of physical activity in A/J but not B6 mice. CA also induced extensive transcriptomic and metabolomic remodeling in muscle, particularly in A/J mice on a standard diet, consistent with activation of energy-dissipating pathways, including sarcolipin-mediated SERCA uncoupling and futile lipid cycling. These findings suggest that CA recruits a persistent muscle NST program in A/J mice that increases whole-body EE, in part by reducing skeletal muscle work efficiency, providing a mechanistic explanation for sustained thermogenesis and resistance to obesity.

papers.title: Psychological well-being in adults with atopic dermatitis: Clinical and psychosocial factors associated with WHO-5 scores in a cross-sectional study of 104 patients.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is associated with impaired quality of life and a substantial psychosocial burden. The World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5) is a validated instrument for assessing subjective psychological well-being. This study investigated psychological well-being and associated clinical and psychosocial factors in adults with AD using the WHO-5. We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 104 adults with AD at a tertiary referral center. Sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, and disease-related clinical measures were assessed using the Scoring Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD) index, Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI), Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure (POEM), and WHO-5. Associations between clinical and psychosocial variables and psychological well-being were examined. The mean age was 39 years, and 44% of participants were women. The mean WHO-5 score was 53 points, indicating moderate-to-low psychological well-being. Lower well-being was associated with unemployment (P < .014), higher educational attainment (P < .026), facial involvement (P < .045), and comorbid anxiety (P = .044). Greater itch severity (P < .001), sleep disturbance (P = .003), higher POEM scores (P < .001), and greater dermatology-related quality-of-life impairment, as measured by the DLQI (P < .001), were also associated with lower psychological well-being. Psychological well-being in adults with AD was associated with socioeconomic characteristics, facial involvement, comorbid anxiety, pruritus, sleep disturbance, and patient-reported disease burden. These findings support integrating psychological well-being assessment into comprehensive AD management and warrant further investigation of interventions targeting both dermatologic symptoms and psychosocial outcomes.

papers.title: Nonverbal reasoning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: associations with gross motor function, MRI, and EEG findings.
papers.abstract: To examine the association between gross motor function level and Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (CPM) performance in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy (CP), compare CPM performance with typically developing participants, and explore associations with MRI and EEG findings. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 40 participants with CP and 20 comparison participants aged 10-17 years. CPM totals were converted to center-derived age-referenced scores; the upper available normative age band was applied above age 11.5 years. Gross motor function was classified with the GMFCS. Clinically indicated MRI and EEG findings were categorized using prespecified systems. Median CPM score was 72 (IQR 64-81) in the CP group and 98 (IQR 92-104) in the comparison group (adjusted difference -26.4, 95% CI -31.2 to -21.6). GMFCS level was inversely associated with CPM score (Spearman rho = -.78, 95% CI -.85 to -.68). Predominant white matter injury was associated with lower CPM scores. The adjusted association with epileptiform EEG abnormalities was inconclusive. CPM performance was associated with GMFCS level and MRI pattern, but the cross-sectional findings do not establish causality. Gross motor classification must not substitute for accessible neuropsychological assessment.
papers.journal: Child neuropsychology : a journal on normal and abnormal development in childhood and adolescence

papers.title: Spectral envelopes of facial movements predict intention, cortical representations, and neural prosthetic control.
papers.abstract: Animals use coordinated facial movements to sample the environment, ingest nutrients, and communicate. Rodents produce rhythmic facial movements during spontaneous behavior and cognitive tasks. Measuring these movements precisely and linking them to neural activity remains challenging. We introduce face-rhythm, an unsupervised pipeline that combines markerless point-tracking, spectral analysis, and non-negative tensor decomposition to reduce facial video to a small set of interpretable components. Applied to videos of mice performing Pavlovian conditioning, a brain-machine interface task, and free behavior, face-rhythm recovers whisking, sniffing, licking, and subtler motifs. The resulting components are consistent across animals, decode task variables and internal states, and explain cortical activity with a low-rank representation. Facial motor cortex neurons are predicted well by a phase-invariant spectral transformation of movements above roughly 0.5 Hz, whereas slower movements retain a phase-variant representation. Face-rhythm compares favorably with deep-learning tracking and embedding methods while yielding an interpretable description of facial behavior.

papers.title: Associations between yoga nidra participation and stress, sleep quality, and academic resilience of nursing students during their first clinical practicum.
papers.abstract: Although mind-body interventions such as yoga nidra may reduce stress and improve emotional regulation, evidence in nursing education remains limited. To examine the associations between yoga nidra participation and changes in practicum-related stress, sleep quality, and academic resilience among nursing students during their first clinical practicum. A cluster-based quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design was employed. Participants were recruited from a junior college in Taiwan. The intervention group participated in structured online yoga nidra sessions delivered via Microsoft Teams four times weekly for four weeks, whereas the control group received only routine educational support. Validated questionnaires assessing practicum stress, sleep quality, and academic resilience were administered at baseline and post-intervention. Group differences were analyzed using ANCOVA and the Johnson-Neyman technique after controlling for baseline scores. The intervention group demonstrated lower posttest practicum stress and higher academic resilience than the control group after baseline adjustment. Significant improvements were also observed in subjective sleep quality, sleep latency, sleep duration, daytime dysfunction, and overall sleep quality. All statistically significant outcomes showed medium-to-large effect sizes (partial η2 = 0.06-0.51). Improvements in workload stress and practicum environment stress were more pronounced among students with higher baseline stress levels. Given the substantial baseline imbalance and limited covariate overlap between groups, findings related to stress and academic resilience should be interpreted cautiously. Nursing students improved their psychological well-being and learning adaptation following the structured online yoga nidra intervention, making it a feasible and low-risk supportive strategy in nursing education settings.

papers.title: Aesthetic preference for the visual appearance of modern decorative cabinets in young adults: An ERP study.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the neural processing underlying aesthetic preferences for the visual appearance of modern decorative cabinets and examined whether cabinets associated with different preference levels elicited distinct event-related potential (ERP) responses. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded from 31 young adults while they viewed modern decorative cabinet images and standardized affective pictures from the Chinese Affective Picture System (CAPS), which served as an affective reference set. Participants rated each image using a 5-point scale. Ratings were recoded into three preference levels for behavioral and ERP analyses. Within-participant consistency and between-participant agreement were assessed using repeated cabinet ratings. Repeated cabinet preference ratings were relatively consistent within participants, whereas agreement between participants was limited. In the frontal region, medium-preference cabinet images elicited significantly larger N100 amplitudes than high- and low-preference images. Late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes did not differ significantly across cabinet preference levels, whereas CAPS images showed significant LPP differences across preference levels. Response times were longer for cabinet images than for CAPS images. The findings highlight the involvement of early perceptual processing in aesthetic preference judgments of modern decorative cabinets. This study provides evidence for understanding the temporal characteristics of furniture appearance evaluation.

papers.title: The impact of mindfulness on sleep, cognitive function and athletic performance of young males migrating to the plateau.
papers.abstract: To examine whether an 8-week mindfulness training program was associated with changes in sleep quality, cognitive function, and athletic performance in young men who migrated to high-altitude regions. Ninety-six young male migrants were randomly assigned to an 8-week mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) program (n = 48) or a no-intervention control group (n = 48). Sleep quality (PSQI), cognitive processing (P300 latency), and athletic performance (3000-m run time) were assessed before and after the intervention. The mindfulness group was associated with greater improvements in sleep quality (PSQI median: 7.5 to 5 vs. 8 to 8.5, P < 0.001) and cognitive processing speed (P300 latency median: 387 ms to 357 ms vs. 376.5 ms to 374.5 ms, P = 0.01) compared with controls. Exploratory analyses suggested that P300 amplitude increased in parietal and occipital regions. No significant between-group difference was observed in 3000-m run completion time (P = 0.51) or grade improvement rates (25.0% vs. 29.17%, P = 0.65). An 8-week mindfulness intervention was associated with improved sleep quality and cognitive processing speed, but no significant association was observed with athletic performance, in young male migrants to high-altitude regions. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of mindfulness as a non-pharmacological strategy for high-altitude health management, pending replication with active control conditions.

papers.title: Temporal associations between dysfunctional sleep beliefs and insomnia severity in CBT-I subcomponents: A randomized dismantling trial.
papers.abstract: Dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs may contribute to the insomnia persistence and change during treatment. However, the temporal ordering of belief and symptom changes, and whether it varies across cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBTI) components, remain unclear. This study examined these processes in a randomized dismantling trial. A total of 120 patients were randomly assigned to CBTI, cognitive therapy for insomnia (CT-I), behavioral therapy for insomnia (BT-I), or treatment as usual (TAU) group. Active interventions were delivered weekly for 8 weeks. The Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) and Brief Version of Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep (DBAS-16) were assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 8. Parallel process latent growth curve models (PP-LGCMs) tested longitudinal mediation. Separate three-wave Cross-Lagged Panel Models (CLPMs) estimated treatment-specific temporal associations. All three interventions reduced insomnia severity and dysfunctional beliefs. PP-LGCMs showed significant indirect effects through dysfunctional beliefs for CBT-I and CT-I, but not BT-I. Dysfunctional beliefs fully mediated treatment effects in CT-I and partially mediated effects in CBTI. CLPMs findings varied by treatment and interval. Week-4 insomnia severity predicted selected belief domains at week 8 in CBT-I and BT-I. In CT-I, baseline medication-related beliefs predicted week-4 insomnia severity, which in turn predicted later total and consequence-related belief scores. Beliefs showed a significant indirect role in CBT-I and CT-I, but not BT-I. Cross-lagged associations were treatment- and interval-specific. Larger studies with more frequent assessments are needed to clarify these pathways and determine whether directly targeting beliefs accelerates symptom improvement.

papers.title: Correlation study between pre-stroke sleep characteristics and early neurological prognosis in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the association between pre-stroke sleep conditions and 3-month functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Consecutive AIS patients admitted between March 2022 and August 2024 were enrolled. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and Berlin Questionnaire were administered within 7 days after stroke onset to evaluate pre-stroke sleep characteristics. Poor functional outcome was defined as a 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score >2. Binary logistic regression was used to identify prognostic factors. Of 782 patients completing follow-up, 18.0% had poor functional recovery. Compared with the good-prognosis group, patients with poor prognosis had a higher rate of pre-stroke excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) and more frequent in-hospital sedative-hypnotic use (both P < 0.05). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that age >65 years, female sex, prior stroke history, higher admission NIHSS score, and pre-stroke EDS were independent risk factors for poor prognosis. Small-artery occlusion was protective relative to large-artery atherosclerosis (OR = 0.36, P = 0.002). Pre-stroke EDS appeared to be independently associated with unfavourable three-month functional outcome, apart from established clinical risk factors. Small-artery occlusion predicts better functional recovery compared with large-artery atherosclerosis.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

papers.title: Success rate of MRI scanning during natural sleep for younger autistic and typically developing toddlers.
papers.abstract: Toddlerhood represents a critical period of brain development in autism, yet there is limited magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data for children ages 1-3 years. These ages are difficult to scan without sedation because toddlers tend to have difficulty falling asleep in noisy, unfamiliar environments and following instructions to stay still. While some studies have successfully scanned typically-developing toddlers without sedation, fewer have scanned autistic toddlers. The few with high success rates (>90%) are not easily replicated (e.g., flexible scan durations). Recent reviews emphasize a need for gold-standard, feasible scan protocols and detailed reporting of natural-sleep methods. To address these gaps, we examined MRI scan success rates and detailed our scanning procedures. Twenty-two autistic and twenty-three typically-developing toddlers attempted scans during natural, non-sedated sleep in our longitudinal study. Our MRI battery included structural, resting-state functional, and diffusion-weighted scans. The overall scan success rate was 40.3%; autism (36.4%) and non-autism groups (44.1%) did not significantly differ. Among unsuccessful scans, 87.5% resulted from toddlers not falling asleep. Success rates did not significantly differ by factors such as age, timepoint, or developmental functioning. While our success rate aligns with most literature describing difficulty scanning 1-3 year-olds, our rate was lower than the few high-rate, natural-sleep studies of autistic toddlers. We identified differences in procedures and budget as key considerations (e.g., absence of standardized pre-visit measures, inability to scan late in evenings). These differences emphasize the need for standardized procedures to bolster success rates and broaden our understanding of early brain development in autism.

papers.title: Association between quantitative REM sleep without atonia and skeletal muscle indices by subsequent phenoconversion status in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: To examine whether associations between quantitative REM sleep without atonia (RWA) and skeletal muscle indices differ by subsequent phenoconversion status in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD). This retrospective study included 114 patients with video-polysomnography-confirmed iRBD (88 non-converters, 26 converters). RWA was manually quantified from submental and bilateral tibialis anterior electromyography across all evaluable REM sleep. Tonic RWA index (RWAI) was scored in 30-s epochs according to SINBAR criteria; total RWAI was the percentage of 3-s mini-epochs containing tonic or phasic activity in any channel. Skeletal muscle mass index (SMI; primary outcome) and fat-free mass index (FFMI) were measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis at diagnosis. Linear regression with robust standard errors tested RWAI-by-phenoconversion interactions, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, apnea-hypopnea index, and regular exercise. Converters had higher tonic, phasic, and total RWAI than non-converters, whereas mean SMI and FFMI were similar. Among converters, total RWAI was inversely correlated with SMI (ρ = -0.61) and FFMI (ρ = -0.54); no such associations were observed among non-converters. In fully adjusted models, the total RWAI-by-phenoconversion interaction was significant for SMI (β = -0.294 per 10 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.513 to -0.076; P = 0.009) and FFMI (β = -0.626; 95% CI, -1.099 to -0.152; P = 0.010). The SMI interaction was robust in most sensitivity analyses. The inverse association between RWA and skeletal muscle indices was more pronounced among patients with iRBD who subsequently phenoconverted. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Pain in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder: Findings from longitudinal and deep-phenotyping cohorts.
papers.abstract: Pain is a common non-motor symptom in Parkinson's disease, yet whether it emerges in the prodromal period and whether it reflects underlying dopaminergic degeneration remains poorly characterized. Our objectives are threefold: to determine whether pain is elevated in polysomnogram-confirmed isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), whether it predicts phenoconversion to overt synucleinopathy, and whether it is associated with regional dopaminergic deficits. Participants with iRBD (n = 507) and demographically-matched controls (n = 33) enrolled in the North American Prodromal Synucleinopathy (NAPS) Consortium from August 2018 through July 31, 2025 were analyzed. Pain was assessed using MDS-UPDRS item 1.9. Cox proportional hazards models - including a time-varying model incorporating repeated assessments - examined pain as a predictor of phenoconversion. Dopamine transporter (DAT) SPECT imaging was performed in a subset (n = 244), and ordinal logistic regression models evaluated associations between regional striatal binding ratios and pain severity. An independently recruited clinically enriched chronic pain cohort (n = 110) with and without RBD underwent detailed pain phenotyping without neuroimaging. Participants with iRBD had significantly higher odds of greater pain severity than controls (OR = 2.24, 95%CI 1.17-4.49, p = 0.02). Moderate-severe baseline pain predicted phenoconversion (HR = 2.21, 95%CI 1.13-4.32, p = 0.02), an estimate that remained stable after adjustment for several medical covariates, although the overall three-category model was not statistically significant (p = 0.08). Cross-sectional striatal DAT binding was not associated with symptom severity. Despite greater subjective pain burden, objective pressure algometry did not differ between iRBD and controls. Pain may represent a prodromal symptom of synuclein-based neurodegeneration but was not associated with striatal DAT binding, suggesting that nigrostriatal terminal loss alone does not explain the association.

papers.title: AI-Based Monitoring Devices for the Identification of Circadian Parameters as Digital Predictive Biomarkers of Neurodegenerative Diseases in Older Adults: Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, and related dementias are a growing health burden among older adults. Circadian disruption is increasingly recognized as both a consequence and a potential early marker of neurodegenerative progression. Wearable sensing combined with AI enables continuous, noninvasive, and ecologically valid monitoring of circadian parameters as potential digital biomarkers. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on AI-enhanced wearable and objective sensing devices used to monitor circadian parameters in older and cognitively vulnerable adults and evaluates their potential as digital predictive biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases. Following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, an original search of PubMed, Scopus, and JMIR journals (June 2025) yielded 12 studies, 7 of which met updated eligibility criteria on rescreening. A complementary search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library (March 24, 2026) added 3 eligible studies and 3 sensitivity references (excluded records retained to delimit the corpus boundary). Two reviewers (JMH-Z and JM-R) independently assessed risk of bias with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Heterogeneous end points precluded meta-analysis; the narrative synthesis covered 4 prespecified domains: device class, circadian construct, AI and machine learning (ML) method family, and population and neurocognitive context. The final corpus comprised 13 records (10 eligible studies and 3 sensitivity references) published from 2015 to 2025. Wrist actigraphy predominated, and samples ranged from community-dwelling older adults to nursing home residents with advanced dementia (n=16-7297). Circadian parameters included interdaily stability, intradaily variability, relative amplitude, midline estimating statistic of rhythm, acrophase, and circadian stimulus. AI/ML methods included supervised learning (random forests, gradient boosting, and regression models), unsupervised clustering, and algorithm development or validation; 7 studies applied deterministic algorithms without fitting a predictive model. Circadian fragmentation was associated with functional decline, dementia risk, and cognitive performance. Most studies were descriptive or observational with small, nondiverse samples; no AI model was externally validated, and no study followed an AI-specific reporting guideline. AI-enhanced wearable devices show meaningful potential for noninvasive measurement of circadian disruption in older and cognitively vulnerable populations. Evidence certainty is moderate for actigraphy-derived fragmentation-function associations in institutional settings and low for predictive biomarker claims in community populations. From 6 recurring challenges along the sensing-to-biomarker pipeline, we propose a 4-layer reference architecture (sensing and acquisition, circadian parameter extraction, AI/ML inference, and a clinical and validation interface) with a layered validation pathway. Longitudinal, multisite validation studies using standardized circadian metrics, diverse populations, and explainable AI remain necessary before clinical deployment as neurodegenerative biomarkers.

papers.title: Safety, Signal Quality, and Patient Satisfaction With Insertable Loop Recorder Implantation by Specialized Electrophysiology Nurses: Prospective Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Insertable loop recorders (ILRs) are subcutaneous cardiac monitoring devices used in the diagnosis of arrhythmias and in the etiological investigation of syncope and cryptogenic stroke. Device miniaturization and procedural simplification have facilitated implantation in ambulatory settings. The involvement of specialized electrophysiology nurses may help meet rising clinical demand, although evidence in our setting remains limited. This study aimed to analyze implantation safety, detection signal quality, adverse events during follow-up, and patient satisfaction when the procedure was performed by specialized nurses. This prospective observational study (the CARDIONURSE study) was conducted in the Arrhythmia Unit of Hospital General Universitario Doctor Balmis between February 2022 and May 2023. Thirty-five patients with a clinical indication for ILR implantation were included. The procedure was performed by 2 specialized nurses under medical supervision. Sociodemographic, clinical, and technical implantation variables were collected, including detection signal amplitude (mV), together with adverse events and follow-up outcomes at 1 and 6 months. Patient satisfaction was assessed using a study-specific questionnaire at 4 time points. Descriptive statistical analysis was performed. Mean age was 71.1 (SD 11.3) years, and 62.9% (22/35) were women. The most frequent indication was syncope (27/35, 77.1%), followed by suspected atrial fibrillation (AF) in cryptogenic stroke (6/35, 17.1%). No objective procedural complications occurred (35/35, 100% of procedures); mild, transient procedural pain was reported in 5.7% (2/35) of patients, and the procedure lasted less than 5 minutes in 74.3% (26/35) of procedures. Mean signal amplitude was 0.45 (SD 0.29) mV, with a visible P wave in 94.3% (33/35) of patients. No wound-related adverse events were recorded among the 85.7% (30/35) of patients with available follow-up data at 6 months; data were unavailable for the remaining 5 patients. A diagnosis was obtained in 20% (6/30) of patients with an available diagnostic outcome at 6 months. Overall, 97.1% (34/35) of patients reported maximum or very high satisfaction with the intervention, and 100% (35/35) with the care received. ILR implantation by specialized electrophysiology nurses in an ambulatory setting is a safe, fast, and technically adequate procedure, with adequate signal quality and high patient satisfaction. These findings support the feasibility of specialized nursing as ILR implanters in similar ambulatory care settings, although confirmation in larger, multicenter studies is warranted before broader implementation.

papers.title: THERM-D uncovers distinct neural mechanisms separating morning and evening body temperature rhythms in Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Animal body temperature rises throughout the day and peaks in the evening, a pattern conserved across diurnal endotherms and ectotherms. However, the mechanisms driving the robust body temperature rhythms (BTRs) remain largely unclear. Here, we developed a machine learning-based platform, Temperature Homeostasis Evaluation of Rhythmicity in Model Drosophila (THERM-D), enabling continuous, high-throughput analyses of BTR. Using THERM-D, we identified robust BTR patterns reflecting flies' morning and evening behaviors and revealed the function of CRYPTOCHROME (CRY)-negative clock neurons. About half of all clock neurons lack CRY, yet their functions are only partially understood. Gal4 drivers targeting CRY-negative neurons demonstrated that these neurons control the morning temperature rise. We further show that separate clock circuits regulate morning and evening BTRs. Thus, THERM-D elucidated the role of CRY-negative clock neurons in BTR and provides a powerful platform for uncovering mechanisms underlying circadian temperature homeostasis.

papers.title: Association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults: A cross-sectional analysis of CLHLS 2017-2018.
papers.abstract: Prior studies have yielded inconsistent findings regarding the interplay between cognitive function, depression, self-care ability, and sleep quality in older adults, necessitating deeper exploration to elucidate these complex associations. This study aimed to examine whether self-care ability mediates the association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms, and whether sleep quality moderates this relationship in Chinese older adults. We analyzed data from 7,580 older adults (aged ≥65 years) participating in a nationwide longitudinal survey in China (CLHLS, 2017-2018 wave). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10). Self-care ability was measured by physical activities of daily living (PADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL). Cognitive function was assessed using the Community Screening Instrument for Dementia (CSI-D). Sleep quality was measured using a single-item self-report question. Moderated mediation analysis was conducted using SPSS PROCESS Macro (Model 4 for mediation; Model 5 for moderated mediation). Self-care ability partially mediated the association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults (indirect effect β = -0.080, 95%CI [-0.114, -0.048]). Sleep quality moderated the direct path between cognitive function and depressive symptoms (β = -0.148, 95%CI[-0.245, -0.051], P < 0.05), such that the inverse association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms was more pronounced among older adults with poorer sleep quality. Of note, the pattern of mean depressive scores across sleep quality categories in descriptive analyses appeared counter-intuitive, which we address in the Discussion in light of the limitations of single-item sleep assessment. Timely interventions aimed at improving self-care ability and sleep quality may be associated with a reduced risk of depression among the Chinese older adults. However, causal inferences cannot be drawn due to the cross-sectional design.

papers.title: Inferring population-level physiologically based model parameters for sleep in infancy and young childhood.
papers.abstract: The sleep patterns of infants and young children differ from adult sleep patterns, with longer duration and multiple bouts per 24 hours. There is also considerable heterogeneity in infant sleep, both between individuals and within individuals across development. While mathematical models have been used to understand the mechanisms that regulate adult sleep, the development of sleep from infancy through early childhood has remained largely unexplored. Here we used an established mathematical model for adult sleep regulation to investigate how the underlying mechanisms of sleep mature from ages 1 month to 5 years, and identify a basis for inter-individual differences at each age. Using a Bayesian approach to estimate joint distributions of model parameters at different ages, we found that: (i) decreases in the rate of accumulation of sleep homeostatic pressure captured the reduction in sleep duration across development; while (ii) increases in the time scale of the sleep homeostatic drive captured the consolidation of sleep into fewer sleep bouts per day across development. In terms of inter-individual differences, we found larger spread in the parameters within the earlier stages of infancy (<1 year). The center and boundaries of the joint distributions evolved with age through the parameter space, converging towards previously described adult parameter values. A bifurcation analysis of the homeostatic time scale parameter revealed that progressive consolidation of sleep occurs through abrupt loss of bouts one at a time, punctuated by narrow intervals of non-entrained (>24-h) cycles. These results establish plausible, population-level trajectories in physiological parameters underpinning maturation of sleep regulation through infancy and early childhood.

papers.title: Associations of meeting the guidelines for 24-hour movement behaviors with depressive symptoms and perceived stress across the first postpartum year.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression and stress have significant consequences for maternal health. While physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep independently influence mental health, their combined effects within the 24-hour movement framework during postpartum are not well understood. A secondary analysis in the Postpartum 24/7 cohort study (n = 50) examined adherence to the 2025 Canadian 24-hour movement behavior guidelines at 3, 6, and 12 months postpartum from device-based and self-reported measures (including a composite score [0-5] representing number of guidelines met). Guideline adherence was associated with self-reported depressive symptoms (Center for Epidemiological Studies-Depression Scale) and perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale). Logistic and linear mixed-effects models evaluated changes in guideline adherence over time and associations with mental health outcomes. The proportion of participants meeting most guidelines remained stable across postpartum, though self-reported sleep duration (44-63%, p = 0.043) and device-measured sleep efficiency (62-80%, p = 0.017) improved over time. Across postpartum, meeting sleep quality guidelines was associated with lower depressive symptoms (β = -2.44, p = 0.002) and perceived stress (β = -3.87, p < 0.001) and avoiding screen time before bed was associated with lower perceived stress (β = -2.43, p = 0.041). Meeting physical activity and sedentary behavior guidelines was not associated with depressive symptoms or perceived stress after adjustment. Considered collectively, each additional guideline met was associated with lower depressive symptoms (β = -0.81, p = 0.02) and perceived stress (β = -1.90, p < 0.001) scores. Sleep quality guidelines were most consistently associated with better postpartum mental health; meeting more 24-hour movement behavior guidelines may confer additive benefits. These findings suggest a 24-hour behavior approach may help promote postpartum mental health.

papers.title: Prevalence and Mental and Physical Health Correlates of Cardiovascular Disease Among Older US Veterans: Results From the 2025-2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study.
papers.abstract: Objective: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, and older military veterans are at particularly high risk. This study aims to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of CVD in a nationally representative sample of older US veterans and identify correlates of CVD and related multimorbidity. Methods: Data were analyzed from 1,944 veterans aged ≥60 years from the 2025-2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study (NHRVS). Weighted z-tests, multivariable logistic regression, and Bonferroni-corrected comparisons assessed CVD prevalence trends relative to the 2019-2020 NHRVS and identified correlates. Results: Overall CVD prevalence was 25.7% (n = 486), unchanged from the 2019-2020 NHRVS (25.2%; P= .69), as were rates of heart disease (19.0% vs 19.2%) and myocardial infarction (8.3% vs 10.1%). Stroke/TIA prevalence was higher in 2025-2026 (6.3% vs 4.5%; P= .005), though comparability was limited by the addition of TIA in the later wave. CVD was associated with significantly higher odds of major depression (odds ratio [OR]= 1.88), gambling disorder (OR = 1.69), sleep disorder (OR = 1.90), and insomnia (OR=1.68) but lower odds of lifetime suicide attempt (OR = 0.31), alongside higher odds of respiratory disease (OR = 1.98), kidney disease (OR = 1.85), and chronic pain (OR = 1.65). Independent correlates included older age (OR = 1.06), male sex (OR = 2.17), hypertension (OR = 1.48), hypercholesterolemia (OR = 1.66), diabetes (OR = 1.98), and cumulative trauma burden (OR = 1.10). Prim Care Companion CNS Disord 2026;28(6):26m04309. Author affiliations are listed at the end of this article.
papers.journal: The primary care companion for CNS disorders

papers.title: Sleep hygiene, caffeine use, and academic performance among university students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Caffeine use is common among university students, but its associations with sleep hygiene and academic performance remain uncertain. This study examined these associations among Palestinian university students. A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted from March 21 to May 28, 2026. Among 379 participants, continuous grade point average (GPA) was available for 354. Measures included estimated caffeine intake, caffeine timing, Sleep Hygiene Index (SHI) score, sleep duration, sleep regularity, and study hours. Associations were assessed using analysis of variance, correlation, and multivariable linear regression. Caffeine intake was entered into the regression model as ln(mg/day + 1). The mean age was 20.71 ± 1.98 years, and 50.1% were female. Mean Sleep Hygiene Score was 23.32 ± 8.34, with acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.775). Estimated caffeine intake averaged 253.5 ± 180.9 mg/day, with a median of 223 mg/day. Sleep Hygiene Score was positively correlated with raw caffeine intake (Pearson r = .282, p < .001; Spearman rho = .310, p < .001) and log-transformed intake (Pearson r = .210, p < .001). Mean GPA was 3.03 ± 0.59. No statistically significant association was detected between GPA and caffeine category (p = .584), log-transformed caffeine intake (r = -.084, p = .116), raw caffeine intake (Spearman rho = -.098, p = .066), or Sleep Hygiene Score (r = -.061, p = .249). In multivariable regression (n = 352, adjusted R² = 0.123), study hours, sleep regularity, sleep duration, academic year, academic major, and smoking status were independently associated with GPA; caffeine intake was not (B = -0.026, 95% CI [-0.071, 0.020], p = .270). Higher estimated caffeine intake was associated with poorer sleep hygiene. No statistically significant association with GPA was detected, although the confidence interval does not exclude a negative association. The cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

papers.title: Dermal α-synuclein seeding in relation to REM sleep behavior disorder across prodromal and Parkinson disease cohorts.
papers.abstract: REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a well-established prodromal manifestation of synucleinopathy and is closely linked to peripheral clinical features in Parkinson disease (PD). Dermal α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) provides a peripheral measure of pathological α-synuclein across these disease stages. We performed a cross-sectional analysis of data from the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), including controls, participants with polysomnography-confirmed RBD, and participants with PD. Skin SAA positivity and participant-level kinetic measures (area under the curve [AUC], maximum fluorescence [Fmax], and time to threshold [TTT]) were assessed at 1:20 and 1:50 lysate dilutions. Participants with PD were further classified as suspected brain/motor-enriched or body/peripheral-enriched based on prespecified exploratory clinical features. Skin SAA positivity was detected in 53.3% of participants with polysomnography-confirmed RBD compared with none of the controls, and RBD participants showed significantly faster amplification than controls at both lysate dilutions. Within PD, binary SAA positivity was higher in the suspected body/peripheral-enriched than brain/motor-enriched phenotype, but the difference was not statistically significant (83.3% vs 47.6%; p = 0.067). All seven kinetic measures were greater in the suspected body/peripheral-enriched phenotype after false discovery rate correction, but these differences were not retained when RBDSQ total score was removed from the classification. RBDSQ total score was the only clinical variable associated with skin SAA kinetics after correction and was significantly associated with six of the seven kinetic measures. These findings show that dermal α-synuclein seeding is detectable in PSG-confirmed prodromal RBD and is associated with RBD-related clinical features within established PD.

papers.title: Joint associations of self-reported restless sleep and depressive symptoms with incident heart disease in older adults: A pooled analysis of 3 prospective cohort studies.
papers.abstract: Restless sleep is an item on the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression (CES-D) scale, so adjusting for a CES-D score partly adjusts for the exposure. Whether sleep complaints are associated with cardiovascular risk independently of depressive symptoms is unclear. We aim to examine separate and joint associations of restless sleep and depressive symptoms with incident heart disease in older adults. We analyzed 18,362 adults aged ≥60 years without reported heart disease from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, the Health and Retirement Study (United States), and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. The baseline CES-D item defined restless sleep and was removed from the depressive-symptom score. Incident heart disease was a self-reported physician diagnosis at later waves. Cohort-specific weighted grouped-time proportional hazards estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis. Over 171,863 person-years, 4906 participants reported incident heart disease. Relative to neither condition, pooled hazard ratios were 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.98-1.16) for restless sleep alone, 1.16 (1.03-1.31) for depressive symptoms alone, and 1.36 (1.20-1.55) for both. The both-conditions estimate was significant in each cohort and similar in most post hoc sensitivity analyses. The estimate for depressive symptoms alone and the contrast between both conditions and depressive symptoms alone were not stable to cohort omission. No clear departure from additivity was detected. In an exploratory analysis restricted to participants without elevated depressive symptoms at 2 assessments 2 years apart, restless sleep reported at both assessments was not clearly associated with incident heart disease (1.15, 95% CI 0.96-1.37). At 7 to 8 years, standardized risk (death treated as censoring) was 4.0 to 7.5 percentage points higher with both conditions than neither. Restless sleep without elevated depressive symptoms was not clearly associated with incident heart disease, whereas its combination with elevated depressive symptoms identified a higher-risk group in every cohort, without evidence of synergy. An independent contribution of restless sleep beyond depressive symptoms was not established. In later life, restless sleep should be interpreted together with depressive symptoms rather than on its own.

papers.title: Effectiveness of mindfulness-based interventions on psychological well-being among nurses: A systematic review of randomized and non-randomized studies.
papers.abstract: Nurses frequently experience psychological well-being challenges in clinical settings, particularly related to burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) are widely implemented to address psychological well-being in nurses. While previous reviews have primarily focused on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), incorporating non-randomized intervention studies may provide complementary evidence from a broader range of clinical settings. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of MBIs on nurses' burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality. We searched PubMed, Medline, Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and CINAHL up to June 2025 to identify RCTs and non- randomized intervention studies addressing the values of mindfulness-based interventions in nurses. A total of 16 studies involving 1124 participants were included, comprising 12 parallel-group randomized controlled trials, one randomized crossover trial, and three non-randomized intervention studies. Study-level findings generally favored MBIs for burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality; however, the magnitude and precision of the reported effects varied across studies, and several findings were nonsignificant. Risk-of-bias assessments ranged from low to critical, and the overall certainty of evidence for all three outcomes was low. The available evidence suggests that MBIs may have beneficial effects on burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality among nurses; however, confidence in these findings remains limited by methodological weaknesses, risk of bias, heterogeneity across studies, and the small evidence base for some outcomes. The non-randomized studies provide complementary information on the application of MBIs in clinical nursing settings but do not strengthen causal inference. Further rigorously designed and adequately powered randomized studies are needed to clarify the magnitude and sustainability of these effects.

papers.title: The effect of physical exercise on sleep quality in Chinese middle school students: A cross-sectional study on the mediating role of positive and negative emotions.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore the effect of physical exercise (PE1) on sleep quality (SQ) among Chinese middle school students and to further analyze the mediating roles of positive and negative emotions (NE). A total of 1056 middle school students (aged 11-15 years, M = 13.28, SD = 1.08; 516 males, 540 females) from 6 middle schools in Sichuan Province, China, voluntarily participated in this cross-sectional survey. The Physical Activity Rating Scale, Positive and Negative Affect Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index were used in this study. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. Mediation analyses (model 4) were conducted with the PROCESS 3.5 macro, and the significance of indirect effects was tested using a bias-corrected nonparametric percentile bootstrap method with 5000 resamples, generating 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The total effect of PE1 on SQ was not significant (P > .05). After controlling for positive and NE, the direct effect of PE1 on SQ was also non-significant (P > .05). However, both positive emotions (indirect effect = 0.032, 95% CI [0.015, 0.051]) and NE (indirect effect = 0.037, 95% CI [0.012, 0.064]) played significant mediating roles in the relationship between PE1 and SQ. These findings suggest that PE1 improves SQ in middle school students primarily by enhancing positive emotions and reducing NE, rather than through a direct effect.

papers.title: Time in psychoanalysis.
papers.abstract: By recognizing the existence of conservative infantile amnesia, psychoanalysis introduced a new category of temporality: timelessness. The contents thus subjected to amnesia escape the influence of time. This unconscious psychic reality is established to counteract the regressive force emanating from the id, in order to fulfil a function: that of thwarting the tendencies to revert to a prior state, even to the inorganic, which are inherent in every drive, and to prevent the disappearance of libidinal cathexes into a 'traumatic timelessness'. Through the regression of sleep, dream work can use this tendency towards extinction to create new psychic content and regenerate narcissistic and object-related cathexis. The dream is the time machine, the fountain of youth available to human beings. The oscillation between experiences of disappearance and those of regeneration, between an endo-perception of discontinuity characterized by experiences of disappearance and eternity, lies at the origin of the notion of temporality, as well as of many devices designed to create the illusion of continuity. Extinction cannot be represented; it is perceived through the traumatic emotions of terror and anxiety. This is why time can only be embodied by the devices that measure it - that is to say, by a method consisting of retaining that which tends to disappear.

papers.title: Blood-derived dietary protein promotes sleep in the mosquito Aedes aegypti.
papers.abstract: Sleep is a ubiquitous, yet highly variable, behavior across species. The duration and timing of sleep are influenced by ecological demands and dietary context. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, a blood-feeding insect with specialized nutritional requirements, the relationship between feeding and sleep remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how blood-derived dietary protein influences sleep regulation. Using postural analysis, videography, and arousal-threshold assays, we established that immobility bouts of ≥10 min reliably define sleep in A. aegypti. Mosquitoes lacking the circadian clock gene cycle still maintained daily sleep rhythms but exhibited reduced sleep duration and heightened overall activity. Infrared activity monitoring revealed that blood-fed females showed a marked increase in sleep beginning immediately after feeding and persisting for several days, accompanied by reduced locomotor activity. Notably, this sleep elevation lasted well beyond the cessation of previously reported host-seeking phases, raising the possibility of distinct phases of opportunistic vs. targeted host pursuit. To determine the dietary basis of this effect, we tested mosquitoes fed a bovine serum albumin (BSA)-based diet. BSA feeding alone was sufficient to mimic the sleep-promoting and activity-reducing effects of blood, suggesting dietary protein is a major nutritional regulator. Moreover, RNAi-mediated knockdown of the leucokinin receptor (Lkr), which has previously been associated with fluid homeostasis and feeding behavior, resulted in enhanced sleep and reduced activity, implicating mosquito LK signaling in the modulation of postprandial sleep. Together, these findings demonstrate that blood-derived proteins drive sustained increases in sleep and reductions in locomotor activity in A. aegypti. This work positions A. aegypti as a model for dissecting nutrient-specific regulation of sleep and highlights potential adaptive functions of protein-induced quiescence, such as energy conservation and predator avoidance. More broadly, it provides insight into how specialized diets shape the neural and behavioral architecture of sleep.

papers.title: Rituximab-responsive epilepsia partialis continua in autoimmune Polyendocrine syndrome: A video-EEG-EMG polygraphic study.
papers.abstract: Epilepsia partialis continua (EPC) is a rare and challenging form of focal motor status epilepticus. Its occurrence strictly in systemic autoimmune disorders without overt encephalitis is exceptional. Corticosteroids are first-line therapy but may be limited by significant side effects and poor metabolic tolerability. We report a 54-year-old woman with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome (APS), including autoimmune hepatitis, latent autoimmune diabetes in adults, celiac disease, and hypothyroidism, presenting with continuous jerks of right III-V fingers. Neurological examination showed continuous, irregular jerks confined to the right III, IV, and V fingers. Extensive serum and CSF screenings, including neuronal antibodies, and MRI were unremarkable. Ictal HMPAO-SPECT revealed a focal hyperperfusion in the left hand-knob area of the primary motor cortex. Brain FDG-PET revealed focal hypometabolism in the same region. Video-EEG-EMG polygraphy showed intermittent spikes and polyspikes over the left central region preceding EMG bursts of the right V finger's abductor muscle with a latency of approximately 30-40 ms. These findings were consistent with EPC. Corticosteroids induced marked improvement but were discontinued due to severe glycemic worsening. Subsequent treatment with oral steroids, IVIG, and multiple antiseizure medications were ineffective. Administration of Rituximab led to complete and sustained clinical and electrophysiological remission, which persisted at the 18-month follow-up. EPC can be a severe, focal manifestation of systemic autoimmunity even without encephalitis. Rituximab represents an effective steroid-sparing option for refractory autoimmune EPC, particularly in metabolically vulnerable patients.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

papers.title: Clinical outcomes and EEG monitoring in absence epilepsy trials: A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Absence epilepsy is characterized by typical absence seizures with distinct electroclinical signatures. The main semiological feature is sudden behavioral arrest associated with brief impairment of consciousness, and the electroencephalographic (EEG) hallmark pattern is generalized, symmetric 2.5-4 Hz spike-and-wave discharges (GSW). Absence epilepsy diagnosis relies on correlating GSW with observable clinical manifestations. Monitoring therapeutic effects based solely on reported symptoms may be misleading, as behavioral arrest can be difficult to identify. Patients often do not recall most seizures, and observable motor/behavioral signs may be subtle, such as minimal twitches or transient lapses in responsiveness, which may go unnoticed. In clinical trials for absence epilepsies, quantification of GSW activity by EEG offers an objective and accurate measure of electrical burden and therapeutic efficacy. Despite technological limitations, GSW remains a robust neurophysiological endpoint. Increasing evidence indicates that the timing and burden of GSW correlate with epilepsy comorbidities, including attention, cognition, behavior, and sleep. We reviewed the published literature regarding GSW as an outcome measure in absence epilepsy, including nonseizure outcomes and comorbidities. Our review highlights (1) nearly 100% of clinical absence seizures exhibit sustained GSW discharges on EEG; (2) >49% of electrographic seizures are asymptomatic, indicating that reliance on seizure diaries without EEG monitoring underestimates seizure frequency and burden; (3) Genetic Generalized Epilepsy is not a benign condition and is associated with a high prevalence of cognitive and behavioral comorbidities, supporting evaluation beyond clinically observable seizures and the use of prolonged (≥24-h) EEG monitoring; (4) circadian and multidien cycles further emphasize the need for prolonged EEG recordings to reduce timing-related bias; and (5) antiseizure medications effective in absence epilepsy reduce GSW, supporting EEG monitoring as an objective treatment outcome measure. We therefore recommend incorporating ≥24-h EEG in future clinical trials, especially in (young) adults, and exploring comorbidities as important outcome measures. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Absence epilepsy causes brief episodes in which a person suddenly stops what they are doing and may not be aware of their surroundings. Many of these seizures have no obvious signs and are often missed or forgotten, meaning seizure diaries alone do not show the full picture. Our review shows that brain recordings (electroencephalographic, EEG), especially when done over 24 h or longer, detect many unrecognized seizures and better measure how well treatments work. EEG findings are also linked to problems with attention, thinking, behavior, and sleep, highlighting the need to look beyond visible seizures when evaluating treatments in clinical trials.

papers.title: LWD1 acts as a mobile regulator of Arabidopsis circadian clock.
papers.abstract: In Arabidopsis, the circadian clock generates ~24-h rhythms that enable plants to anticipate daily environmental changes. Increasing evidence shows that different tissues have distinct rhythmic programs, and the vascular-tissue clocks are viewed as the central hubs that asymmetrically regulate neighboring tissues via mobile signals. However, the identities and roles of these signals remain largely elusive. We previously reported that Arabidopsis mutants defective in LWD1 and LWD2 have a shortened ~18-h period length and reduced amplitude, indicating LWD1 and LWD2 are required for a stable and robust clock. Here we show that the promoters of LIGHT-REGULATED WD1 (LWD1) and LWD2 are preferentially active in vascular tissues. Our data support that LWD1 acts as a mobile factor that migrates cell-to-cell and tissue-to-tissue to regulate the circadian clock in neighboring or distal parts of the plant body. Results indicate that LWD1 mobility is driven, at least in part, by LWD1 mRNA moving from vascular tissue into adjacent mesophyll cells, where it can function in regulating the circadian clock. Grafting experiments further demonstrate long-distance movement of shoot-derived LWD1 mRNAs to the roots of the lwd1 lwd2 mutant and partially rescue the circadian defects in lwd1 lwd2 roots. Taken together, LWD1 mRNAs can be mobile signaling molecules that coordinate circadian communication locally and systemically in Arabidopsis.

papers.title: Lp(a) Lowering, a GLP-1 Drug for Sleep Apnea, Stopping Statins in Older Age, and More From AHA 2026.
Intrarater reliability of expert electroencephalographic interpretation of 100 full-length recordings.
papers.abstract: The value of electroencephalography (EEG) relies on accurate and reliable interpretation. Prior research has demonstrated imperfect interrater reliability, but intrarater reliability remains poorly characterized. We performed a "noise audit" primarily to measure intrarater variability in EEG interpretation by epileptologists. Experts independently rated the same 100 full-length EEGs on two separate occasions ≥60 days apart, unaware the EEGs were the same. EEGs were recorded from adult (56%) and pediatric patients in outpatient (78%) and non-critical care inpatient settings. There were 20 studies in each of five categories: normal, focal epileptiform (FE), generalized epileptiform (GE), focal nonepileptiform (FNE), and generalized nonepileptiform (GNE) abnormalities. EEGs were presented using our online platform (EEGHub) without clinical information except for age and sex. Experts rated each recording and indicated their level of confidence (LOC) for each EEG and overall. We analyzed percent as well as chance-corrected intra- and interrater agreement. Fourteen experts (mean of 19 years EEG reading experience, range = 4-52 years) were included in the study. Percent self-agreement was 96% for GE, 90% for FE, 88% for FNE, and 87% for GNE abnormalities; 90% for any epileptiform abnormality; and 82% for any nonepileptiform abnormality. Self-agreement was strongly correlated with interrater agreement (mean κML), which was almost perfect for GE (.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .87-.94) and FE (.82, 95% CI = .77-.87) and substantial for GNE (.75, 95% CI = .69-.81) and FNE (.74, 95% CI = .68-.80) abnormalities. LOC correlated with self-agreement on the presence of nonepileptiform but not epileptiform abnormalities. We found generally strong within-expert agreement in EEG interpretation, especially in the identification of epileptiform abnormalities. Nevertheless, the number of flipped decisions was high enough to be clinically consequential. This undesired variability ("occasion noise") may be addressed by interventions to (1) decrease this noise directly and (2) reduce case ambiguity with longer recordings and better EEG data whenever feasible.

papers.title: Prevalence and Associations of Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in Age Related Macular Degeneration and Other Macular Diseases.
papers.abstract: Older people with visual impairments are at risk of poor mental health and often do not seek mental health support. This study investigated the prevalence and associations of depression and anxiety in people with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and other macular diseases. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among people with AMD and other macular diseases in Australia. Key outcomes of depression and anxiety were measured using the 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15) and the 7-item Generalised Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7). Associations between symptoms of depression and anxiety and clinical, demographic and psychosocial variables were explored in multivariable logistic regression analyses, with multiple imputations for missing data. A total of 1364 responses were analysed. The mean age (SD) of the participants was 79.9 years (9.1) and 68.2% were female. Depressive symptoms (GDS-15 > 5) were present in 15.7% and anxiety (GAD-7 > 4) in 20.8% of participants; over half of those with depressive or anxiety symptoms received no mental health support. Fair/worse self-rated vision [adjusted odds ratio: 2.4 (95% confidence interval:1.5-3.9); p < 0.0001], fair/worse self-rated health [2.4 (1.6-3.6); p < 0.001], high falls concern [2.8 (1.5-5.5); p = 0.002], fair/poor sleep quality [1.7 (1.1-2.7); p = 0.02], loneliness [3.3 (2.1-5.1); p < 0.0001], social isolation [2.8 (1.7-4.5); p < 0.0001] and anxiety [6.9 (4.4-10.7); p < 0.0001] were associated with increased odds of depressive symptoms. Older participants (>75 years) had lower odds of anxiety [0.45 (0.3-0.65); p < 0.0001]. High falls concern [2.38 (1.48-3.83); p < 0.0001), fair/worse sleep quality [1.91 (1.35-2.69); p < 0.0001], loneliness [3.54 (2.43-5.15); p < 0.0001] and depressive symptoms [6.14 (3.96-9.53); p < 0.0001] were associated with increased odds of anxiety. Depressive and anxiety symptoms among older adults with macular disease are both associated with loneliness, high falls concern and poor sleep quality. The multifactorial nature of mental health outcomes highlights the need for holistic, patient-centred care that incorporates mental health screening and appropriate referral pathways.
papers.journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

papers.title: Association of sleep disturbances with poor asthma control in children: Unveiling a hidden burden.
papers.abstract: Asthma is a prevalent chronic condition in children and has been associated with sleep disturbances. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of sleep disturbances in children with asthma and to identify the clinical predictors of impaired sleep quality. The study included children aged 6-16 years with asthma who were followed at the Pediatric Allergy and Immunology Department of Ankara Bilkent City Hospital. A control group of participants with comparable age and demographic characteristics and without any history of chronic, allergic, or psychiatric conditions was also recruited. Sleep disturbances were assessed using the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC), while asthma control was evaluated using the Childhood Asthma Control Test (C-ACT) or ACT. Asthma severity and treatment steps were categorized according to the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA). A total of 210 children diagnosed with asthma (mean age: 11.2 ± 3.4 years; 54.3% male) were included in the study. According to the SDSC, 45.2% of children with asthma had clinically significant sleep disturbances. Compared to healthy controls (n = 199), asthmatic children had significantly higher total SDSC scores [63 (IQR: 50-74) vs. 53 (46-61); p < 0.001] and all subscale scores (p < 0.001). Among asthmatic children, poor asthma control, GINA Step ≥3 treatment, and asthma exacerbations within the last six months were significantly associated with sleep disturbances. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, ACT/C-ACT scores were identified as independent predictors of sleep disturbance, with higher scores associated with lower odds of sleep disturbance (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11-0.35; p < 0.001). Poor asthma control was strongly associated with sleep impairment. Routine assessment of sleep quality could support asthma management in pediatric populations.

papers.title: Factors Associated With Sleep Quality and Insomnia in Caregivers of Persons Living With Dementia.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSleep disturbances are common among caregivers of persons with dementia and can compromise health and caregiving capacity. This study examined factors associated with caregivers' sleep quality and insomnia.MethodsBaseline data from a randomized controlled intervention trial (N = 187; mean age 64.4 years; 71.7% female; 63.1% spousal caregivers) were analyzed. Caregivers completed measures of sleep, psychological functioning, and care-recipient symptoms. Automatic linear modeling with AICC selection identified correlates of sleep quality and insomnia.ResultsMean PSQI (6.6) indicated poor sleep quality; mean ISI (8.2) reflected subthreshold insomnia Perceived stress and care-recipient neuropsychiatric symptoms were associated with both outcomes. Depressive symptoms and caregiver burden were uniquely associated with sleep quality; anxiety, dyadic strain, and caregiver reactions to behavioral symptoms with insomnia. Models explained 39.9% and 47.8% of variance, respectively.ConclusionCaregiver sleep quality and insomnia reflect overlapping psychological and caregiving factors, supporting interventions addressing caregiver distress and care-recipient neuropsychiatric symptoms to improve sleep.
papers.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society

papers.title: More Than a Tobacco Problem: Cigarette Smoking as a Marker of Poorer Cardiovascular Health Among Emergency Medical Services Clinicians.
papers.abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) work demands physical capacity, sustained alertness, and performance under stress, making cardiovascular health a workforce concern, not only a personal one. Cigarette smoking persists in portions of the EMS workforce, but whether it signals cardiovascular risk beyond tobacco exposure itself is unknown. We examined whether cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across the non-tobacco domains of the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework among nationally certified EMS clinicians. We conducted an observational study and cross-sectional secondary analysis of a voluntary survey offered to nationally certified emergency medical technicians (EMTs), advanced EMTs, and paramedics upon completion of recertification (October 2023-April 2024). To isolate associations beyond tobacco exposure, the primary outcome was a modified composite score (mLE7) averaging the seven non-nicotine LE8 domains (0-100 scale). Ideal cardiovascular health was defined as mLE7 ≥ 80. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, educational, occupational, and organizational characteristics. Among 36,436 survey respondents, 7,703 had complete data for smoking status and all seven non-nicotine domains. Of these, 48.8% had never smoked, 45.2% formerly smoked, and 6.0% currently smoked. Mean mLE7 scores were 59.2 among never smokers, 56.9 among former smokers, and 51.5 among current smokers. Compared with never smokers, current smokers had lower adjusted mLE7 scores (β, -6.02; 95% CI, -7.63 to -4.41) and lower odds of ideal cardiovascular health (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.61). Former smokers had intermediate results (β, -1.62; 95% CI, -2.37 to -0.87; aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.86). Current smoking was associated with poorer scores across diet, physical activity, sleep, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose domains (p < 0.05). Clinicians at private and hospital-based agencies had lower adjusted mLE7 scores than those at fire-based agencies. Among EMS clinicians, current cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across nearly every non-tobacco domain, suggesting that smoking may serve as a readily identifiable marker of broader cardiovascular risk in this workforce. Agencies may consider pairing cessation support with broader cardiovascular health initiatives for clinicians who smoke. Sensitivity analyses addressing missing data yielded consistent results.

papers.title: Smartphone use patterns and physical and behavioral health outcomes in undergraduates during the COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.abstract: Objective: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted routines and mental health among college students. We analyzed College Experience Study data combining passive smartphone sensing and weekly Ecological Momentary Assessments to examine behavioral and mental health changes during Winter and Spring 2020 relative to prior years and associations with phone use. Methods: Analyses included 184 participants categorized as low (≤2 hrs/day), moderate (>2-4 hrs/day), or high (>4 hrs/day) users. Results: The initial pandemic period was marked by reduced walking and increased sleep. Phone-use groups differed significantly in walking and sleep: moderate users walked more than low users, while lower-use participants slept more than moderate- and high-use participants. Groups did not differ in PHQ-4 scores, stress, or social activity. Greater phone use was associated with shorter sleep and, exploratorily, lower social activity. Conclusions: These findings suggest that phone use may reflect meaningful differences in students' daily behavioral patterns rather than broad differences in distress during the pandemic.
papers.journal: Journal of American college health : J of ACH

papers.title: Lived experiences of fatigue in individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is a prominent and burdensome symptom of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Its measurement is difficult due to limited definition of the characteristics of fatigue unique to ALS. We aimedto characterize the lived experience of fatigue in ALS, including how it is perceived, understood and experienced, to inform a disease-specific, patient-centred conceptual framework. We developed an interview guide based on existing fatigue scales, review of the literature on fatigue in ALS and the experiences of ALS care providers. We conducted focus groups of people with ALS with open-ended discussion of the fatigue experience. Thematic analysis with a phenomenological approach was employed to identify primary themes. Four focus groups were held with a total of fifteen participants. People reported that fatigue shaped their daily activity and sleep patterns, was worsened by activity and improved with rest, changed social interactions, incorporated mental, physical and emotional components, and was manageable with various means of physical and psychological coping. Some participants reported difficulty distinguishing between physical weakness from ALS and physical fatigue. We identified four interconnected themes that illuminate how fatigue is experienced, interpreted, and given meaning in the everyday lives of people with ALS, extending beyond traditional clinical characterizations. This work has informed development of a conceptual model and a preliminary patient-informed definition of fatigue in ALS. Participants defined fatigue as an all-encompassing phenomenon that feels unique to ALS, is related to weakness, and has physical and mental components only partially managed through rest, expectation-setting and activity modulation.

papers.title: From Symptoms to Burden: Multidomain Phenotyping of Temporomandibular Disorders in Young Adults.
papers.abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are heterogeneous conditions with multifactorial origins. Symptom presence alone provides limited insight into patient impact; burden-based frameworks offer more patient-centred characterization. To compare biopsychosocial characteristics of young adults with and without TMD symptoms, examine burden differences across pain-related (PT), intra-articular (IT) and combined (CT) subtypes, and evaluate associations among TMD burden, somatic symptoms, psychological distress, sleep quality and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL). A cross-sectional study of 540 young adults (aged 19-24), recruited from a university via intranet and peer referrals, employed validated instruments. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests; associations were examined with Spearman's correlations and multivariable regression (α = 0.05). TMD symptoms were reported by 35.6% of participants, with 28.6% describing them as bothersome. Affected individuals were more often female and exhibited higher somatic burden, greater psychological distress and poorer OHRQoL (all p < 0.001). CT cases bore the highest burden, with over half reporting bothersome symptoms, consistently surpassing PT and IT across somatic, psychological and OHRQoL domains. Somatic burden correlated moderately with psychological distress (rs = 0.475). Regression analyses showed OHRQoL significantly associated with TMD burden (B = 0.36), while somatic burden was linked to psychological distress (B = 0.40), sleep quality (B = 0.08) and OHRQoL (B = 0.21). Models explained 14% and 31% of variance, respectively. Burden-based phenotyping highlights CT as the most impacted subtype and underscores the interplay of somatic, psychological and quality-of-life factors. These findings support integrated, multidomain approaches to TMD management in young adults.

papers.title: Circadian Regulation of Gastrointestinal Physiology and Disease: Mechanisms, Chrononutrition, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal physiology varies across the 24-h day as central and peripheral clocks coordinate metabolism, epithelial renewal, mucosal immunity, barrier permeability, motility, and microbial activity. Disrupted temporal organization is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma. This narrative review integrates molecular mechanisms with clinical evidence, distinguishing experimental causality from observational associations. Chrononutrition examines interactions between eating patterns and circadian biology, including meal timing, frequency, regularity, and eating-window duration. Human studies support effects of meal timing on peripheral rhythms, but improvements in metabolic markers do not consistently exceed those achieved by calorie restriction. Sleep disturbance predicts disease activity in some inflammatory bowel disease cohorts, whereas preliminary sleep-intervention trials have not established prevention of relapse. Chronomodulated chemotherapy illustrates both potential benefits and implementation barriers, including sex-dependent outcomes and the need for programmable infusion systems. Chronotype, an individual's preference for earlier or later sleep and activity, may modify the feasibility of temporal interventions. Translation requires adequately controlled trials that assess biological phase, disease activity, nutritional safety, adherence, and clinically meaningful outcomes alongside standard care.

papers.title: Effect of enrichment, stocking density and breed on feather corticosterone, feather dehydroepiandrosterone (sulphate) and their ratio in broiler chickens.
papers.abstract: 1. Understanding how husbandry practices affect chronic stress in broiler chickens is crucial to improve animal welfare.2. This study examined the separate and combined effects of environmental enrichment, stocking density and breed on feather corticosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone (sulphate) (DHEA(S)). These are two endocrine indicators of (long-term) stress.3. In four separate 2⨯2 factorial design experiments in Poland and two separate 2⨯2 factorial design experiments in the Netherlands, broilers with different growth rates were reared under different housing conditions. These varied in enrichment types and stocking densities, representing both conventional and less intensive conditions.4. Feather corticosterone concentrations were elevated in broilers housed without environmental enrichment and/or at higher stocking densities. However, feather corticosterone was not elevated in the faster growing breeds, but rather was lower or there was no genotype effect. The effects of enrichment, stocking density, breed and their interactions were less clear for feather DHEA(S) patterns and the corticosterone/DHEA(S) ratio.5. The results suggested that, while enrichment and stocking density clearly affected stress, the role of DHEA(S) remains complex and poorly understood.6. Further research is needed to confirm if DHEA(S) in feathers is a reliable biomarker of chronic stress in broiler chickens.

papers.title: Frontotemporal Slow-Frequency Dominance in Quantitative EEG as a Potential Biomarker of Post-COVID Cognitive Dysfunction.
